Cassian: "No." Oric stiffened.

Cassian: "Shoulder with me." Oric stared.

Cassian: "Unless you object to my technique."

That was Cassian's kindness: disguising dignity as competence. Oric moved beside him.

Leon held Cael until the last possible second.

Then he let Cassian and Oric take one side, Nera and Maelin the other. Rhea walked ahead with the protection seal. Aira carried the sequence copy. Mira carried the amendment. I carried nothing.

That was harder than carrying.

Elira saw me watching my empty hands.

She was still on the healer cot Maelin had unfolded from the field case, pale under three layers of warming cloth, lips cracked from returning to a body that had not expected her back.

Elira: "Do not make empty hands mean refusal." I looked at her.

Elira: "Sometimes they mean other people are allowed."

The Black Circle moved behind me like a thought too large for language.

Haru: "I know."

Elira: "Know it slower." So I did.

Cael left the chapel through the old west arch.

The academy had gathered beyond the sealed line.

Students filled the stairwell, the upper landing, the corridor beyond it, every place close enough to witness and far enough to be kept from interfering. No one spoke when the seal opened. They saw the body.

They saw who carried him: Cassian, Oric, Nera, and Maelin rather than Noctis faculty or Aurelis officials.

Leon walking behind with both hands empty and shaking.

Aira holding paper like it weighed more than stone.

Mira with ink across her wrist and tears drying unevenly on her face.

Rhea in front, not hiding the dead behind authority.

The first sound came from a Green Circle first-year I did not know. First-year: "His name?" No one rebuked him. Leon answered.

Leon: "Cael Nox."

The boy repeated it, and then someone else did. His name moved through the corridor as correction rather than chant or spectacle.

Cael Nox moved through the academy one voice at a time because the world had spent too long making him conduit, witness, transfer, asset, protected student, return route, and proof.

His name needed the corridor first.

The third hour belonged to me because everyone else had finally been given work.

That was when the danger sharpened.

As long as Elira needed me to hold still, I could hold still. As long as Cael's body was in the room, grief had a center outside me. As long as Rhea issued orders and Maelin corrected breathing and Mira copied sequence, I could become one task among many.

When the chapel thinned, the Black Circle remembered it had no small shape.

The rings widened until silver runes touched the upper arch.

Stone dust lifted from the floor.

Every broken fragment of the Wounded City tried to arrange itself into a diagram around my feet. Halden saw first.

Professor Halden: "Everyone out."

Haru: "No."

My voice did not sound like mine.

It sounded like a door closing under a mountain. Halden froze.

I made myself look at him.

Haru: "If everyone leaves, the room becomes only me." He understood. Too quickly for comfort.

Professor Halden: "Then fewer. Not none." Rhea remained.

Maelin remained because Elira remained.

Elira remained because moving her would be worse.

Aira remained because someone had to count what fear tried to blur.

Mira remained by accident at first, then on purpose when she realized leaving would make her final copy incomplete.

Halden remained with his case closed. Six witnesses.

Not the same as the door.

Enough to keep the room from becoming an altar.

The Black Circle did not like enough. It wanted exact. It wanted whole.

It wanted a rule large enough to hold grief without leaking.

There was no such rule.

That was the third hour's lesson.

I stood in the broken chapel and felt every possible correction within reach. The relay network could be sealed. Noctis could be exposed in every private chamber at once. Lucien's name could be tied to Dominion Severance with a precision no lawyer could soften. Every student carrying a hidden return phrase could be found, marked, shielded, extracted. Every Councilor already drafting containment language could be shown the consequence of asking whether I was safe before asking who had died.

I could do so much good that no one would be able to refuse the shape of it. That was the terror.

Not that I wanted harm.

That I wanted obedience wearing the face of mercy.

Elira's voice reached me from the cot.

Elira: "Tell me one thing you are not doing." I turned my head.

She looked exhausted beyond anything I had language for.

Still, her eyes were clear.

Haru: "I am not closing the relays that already closed."

Elira: "Good. Another."

Haru: "I am not repairing your wounds without Maelin's instruction." Maelin's hands paused. Only for a second.

Elira: "Another."

Haru: "I am not finding Lucien."

The chapel lights bent hard enough to whine. Aira wrote faster.

Elira: "Another."

Haru: "I am not making the world understand before it chooses to listen." That one broke something. Not in the room. In me. The rings slowed.

I had thought restraint meant not acting. It did not.

Restraint meant naming the action I was refusing clearly enough that refusal could become real.

Mira's pencil scratched through silence.

Mira: "Can I record that?" I almost laughed.

It would have been terrible.

It would have been human.

Haru: "Yes." I met their gaze without looking away. Mira wrote:

**Haru Aerlen declined to make the world understand before it chose to listen.**

Rhea read the line.

President Valmont: "That sentence will become a legal problem."

Aira: "Most honest sentences do."

Halden looked at the Black Circle without the old hunger for classification.

Professor Halden: "It may also become a safeguard definition."

Haru: "Do not make me a definition tonight."

He bowed his head once.

Professor Halden: "Recorded."

The fourth hour did not belong to anyone. It was waiting.

Elira slept because Maelin finally made her. Aira left to carry copies to the first protection table and came back with three more pages, two reports, and a honey cake someone had pressed into her hands without a label. She stared at it.

Aira: "Who gives emergency cake without documentation?"

Mira, still copying, said, "Someone kind?"

Aira looked offended by the lack of system and grateful enough to cry again.

She broke it into pieces anyway. No ceremony. No speeches.

Food passed through the room in uneven fragments. Rhea took one bite because Aira glared at her. Halden forgot he was holding his until Cassian returned and told him cake did not become research if observed long enough. Leon came back last.

His hands had been washed. That made it worse.

He stood inside the chapel door and looked at Elira sleeping, then at me, then at the Black Circle still turning above the floor.

Leon: "I hated you once because I thought you were pretending to be weak." No one moved.

Leon: "I was wrong."

Haru: "I was pretending." Leon shook his head.

Leon: "No. You were trying not to become what people like me respect too easily."

The sentence was not elegant.

It was better than elegant.

It had been paid for.

He looked at Cael's absence and swallowed hard.

Leon: "Do not let them turn him into the reason you stop trying."

Then he left before I could answer.

The fifth hour belonged to the first wrong story.

It arrived through a Council emergency relay, not official enough to be addressed and not private enough to ignore.

**BLACK CIRCLE MANIFESTATION CAUSES STUDENT FATALITY DURING UNSANCTIONED RESPONSE**

Rhea read it. The chapel went cold.

Aira said a word that would never survive formal minutes. Mira's face changed. Not fear this time. Offense.

She stood so quickly her chair scraped.

Mira: "No."

Rhea: "Mira."

Mira: "No."

She took the public sequence copy, slapped it onto the relay table, and underlined three lines hard enough to tear the top page.

**ELIRA VALE KILLED BEFORE BLACK CIRCLE MANIFESTATION.**

**CAEL NOX ACTIVATED VOTIVE RETURN AFTER DOMINION SEVERANCE.**

**BLACK CIRCLE EVENT FOLLOWED CATASTROPHIC WITNESS BREACH.**

Mira: "If they want to lie, make them step over the order."

Rhea looked at her for one long second.

President Valmont: "Send it."

The correction went out with Mira's handwriting visible.

That mattered because typed words looked institutional, and institutions were already preparing to fight over authority. Mira's handwriting looked like a person who had watched and refused to let sequence be stolen while the floor was still wet from thawed frost.

The wrong story did not vanish. Wrong stories rarely did.

But it had to drag the correction behind it.

That was enough for the fifth hour.

The sixth hour ended without drama. No burst of darkness. No final bell.

No clean return to secrecy.

The Black Circle slowed until its outer rings became shadow, then pressure, then the old cold behind my sternum. One inner ring remained as a hair-thin mark beneath the skin. The false Green crest did not return on its own. I had to rebuild it with shaking hands while the people in the room watched me choose smallness after everyone had seen the truth.

That was different from hiding. It had to be.

Elira woke as the final ring thinned to shadow.

Her eyes found my wrist. No Green yet. No black blaze either.

Only a hairline darkness beneath the skin, easy to miss and impossible for her not to see.

For one heartbeat, I looked like someone the world had not classified.

Elira reached for my hand.

I gave it to her.

She turned it palm up and rested two fingers against the center, where no crest showed.

Elira: "There you are."

Lucien had said those words like discovery meant possession.

Elira said them like presence was enough. I held still. Not counting breaths. Listening to hers.

Small, real, and enough to begin again.

The room did not forgive me.

It did not need to.

It only let me remain answerable inside it, breathing beside the people who had refused to become symbols for my grief.

---

## Interlude: Aira - The Part That Gets Written

Aira Solen had always trusted records less than people assumed.

She made records for that exact reason.

A record was not truth. It was a chair placed in a room where truth might be allowed to sit before stronger people arrived with better shoes and called it something else.

She had learned that early.

Not in a grand tragedy. Aira disliked grand tragedies. They gave adults too much opportunity to sound meaningful afterward.

She learned it in small rooms where someone said obviously, and everyone else nodded because obviously was easier than asking who had benefited from the answer. She learned it from attendance marks that made absence look identical whether a student was sick, afraid, punished, or simply too poor to afford the carriage after a ward fee changed. She learned it from teachers who remembered bright students by name and Green Circle students by seating row.

So Aira wrote things down.

At first because she was good at it.

Later because being good at something was safer than admitting she needed it to matter.

Haru was on his knees with the Black Circle breaking the world open around him, and Aira's first instinct was still sequence.

That frightened her more than the rings.

Some people screamed when the impossible arrived. Some ran. Some prayed. Aira found the nearest sentence with a missing subject and tried to repair it before the room used the gap.

Useful, accurate, and possibly unbearable.

She did not write because Haru needed protecting. Not only.

She wrote because Elira's body was on the ground, because Cael was being turned into grammar, because Lucien would steal the first story if no one pinned the order down quickly enough, and because someone had to be the person who did not look away long enough to become kind.

That last part was the problem.

Aira had been that person often enough that no one asked whether she wanted the role.

She did not ask either.

Questions like that were inefficient during catastrophe. Also dangerous.

If she asked what it cost her to become the room's memory, she might discover the answer had been accumulating for years in margins she had labeled later. Haru heard her.

The floor under Elira stopped splitting. Mira wrote the proof.

Aira watched the sentence appear and felt something in her chest fold itself into a smaller shape so it could keep functioning. Good; that was Haru. Record that. She did.

And did not, for one more crisis, ask who would record what it cost her to keep recording.

## Aira's Margin - The Night Before the Final Stage

The night before the final stage, Aira wrote the clean record first because clean records survived committees.

Then she wrote the margin record because clean records lied by omission even when every sentence was true.

Margin: Haru has not slept. Elira is pretending pain is a scheduling concern. Leon keeps counting Cael's exits for him and then pretending he was looking at architecture. Cassian brought food no one asked for and placed it where people could reach without gratitude. Rhea is colder when frightened. Valen is gentler when furious.

Aira paused, chewing the end of her pen.

Then she added: If we survive this, do not let the official version make us sound braver than we were. Fear was present. So was love. So was confusion. None invalidate witness.

The margin ink dried crooked.

Aira closed the notebook only when the infirmary clock struck three and everyone flinched except Elira, who had finally fallen asleep.

That, too, went in the margin.

===== EPISODE 14 =====

# Episode 14: **The Vigil**

The infirmary clock struck three before I understood that the day had continued without my permission.

Elira slept on Maelin's cot beneath three warming cloths, one hand open near the edge as if even unconscious she expected someone to need proof that she had returned by choice. Cael had been carried to the eastern preparation room under Rhea's seal. Leon went with him. Nera and Oric went too. I had remained because Maelin asked me to hold the Black Circle still until Elira's channels stopped trying to remember death.

The circle no longer filled the chapel, but its reflection turned behind me in every dark pane. Hiding it was impossible now. Letting it exist witho.

Aira sat beneath the infirmary clock with two notebooks open across her knees. One held the clean sequence. The other held handwriting that leaned harder whenever she was angry.

She closed the second notebook when she saw me watching the relay windows brighten beyond the ward glass.

Haru: "How much happened outside?"

Aira: "Enough that answering with a number would be dishonest."

She studied my face, then turned both notebooks backward through the hours I had survived without seeing.

Aira: "You held Elira's space. We held everything trying to enter it."

Haru: "Start where I stopped looking."

Her finger settled on the first public relay entry.

Aira: "Midmorning."

---

The world could not wait for us to finish grieving. The relay windows had shown too much.

Every academy, council branch, and public record office with a functioning crystal had seen the Black Circle, Elira's death, Cael's choice, Noctis' coercive doctrine, and the old Aurelis warning not to isolate the safeguard.

By midmorning, messages had gathered above the Wounded City chamber like storm clouds made of formal language.

Rhea did not read them aloud at first; she sorted them. Fear made some people reach for chains. Rhea reached for categories.

Requests arrived for medical status, witness confirmation, Noctis comment, Black Circle containment-and Black Circle worship.

That last category made Aira put both hands over her face.

Aira: "No. Absolutely not. We are not doing myth clubs today."

Cassian set another stone aside.

Cassian: "Only today?"

Aira: "Do not make me assign you to public relations while I am this emotionally available to violence." Cassian looked at Cael.

His smile did not come.

Cassian: "Fair."

Rhea dismissed the worship requests without comment and archived every containment request. I noticed. So did Elira.

President Valmont: "Evidence." Her voice was flat.

President Valmont: "Anyone who thought the first official response to a grieving student should be containment may explain that instinct in daylight later." Mira wrote that down.

Finn's mouth bent in a grim line.

Finn: "Green Circle students are copying the archive twice." Rhea looked up.

President Valmont: "Three times." Finn blinked.

President Valmont: "Institutions misplace inconvenient paper. Students misplace nothing when annoyed." Mira's pencil paused.

Mira: "Was that a compliment?"

Rhea: "It was an instruction." Mira wrote faster.

The next message came sealed in silver and violet. Inter-National Schools Council. Magistra Senna Voss.

The chamber changed when her name appeared, though neither trust nor the discomfort of her surname had become simple.

A council registry line opened beneath her name before anyone could weaponize the question.

**SENNA VOSS: NORTHERN CIVIL SERVICE LINE**

**NO DECLARED BLOOD OR HOUSE AFFILIATION WITH LUCIEN VOSS**

That did not make suspicion vanish.

It gave suspicion a place to stand where it could be watched.

Because she had been sent to observe risk and had watched a student die proving where the risk lived.

The message unfolded into a recorded statement.

Senna stood in a council office with no decoration behind her except a wall of floating case files. Her hair was pinned neatly. Her face looked older than it had two days earlier.

Magistra Voss: "This preliminary report is entered under emergency witness priority."

Her eyes moved once, as if reading from a text she had already memorized and hated needing.

Magistra Voss: "I was dispatched to evaluate institutional instability surrounding Aurelis, Noctis Dominion College, and the contested Foundation Witness Trial."

The file panes behind her brightened.

Magistra Voss: "What I witnessed was not a spontaneous threat event. It was a sequence."

Mira's pencil stopped for the first time all morning.

Magistra Voss: "A student under Noctis doctrine was targeted through reclamation pressure. A second student intervened to prevent that harm. Dominion Severance killed her. Votive Return, a doctrine tied to fatal conduit expenditure, restored her at the cost of Cael Nox's life. The Black Circle manifested after the death event, under visible grief pressure, and did not attack witnesses despite ample capacity to do so."

The Black Circle behind me dimmed by a degree because sequence had weight, not because it liked being described.

Magistra Voss: "The risk before this Council is not the existence of power beyond Yellow classification. The risk is the institutional reflex to isolate, claim, spend, or destroy students when ordinary categories fail."

Rhea's hand closed around the edge of her sleeve.

Magistra Voss: "I recommend immediate protection of all Aurelis witnesses, suspension of Noctis final conduit clauses across member jurisdictions pending full investigation, emergency review of Dominion Severance as unlawful coercive magic, and explicit prohibition on isolated classification proceedings concerning Haru Aerlen." She paused.

For one moment, the formal mask thinned.

Magistra Voss: "If the Council's first act after Cael Nox's death is to ask how to contain the student he died beside, my resignation will be submitted before sunset." The message ended. Silence followed.

Aira wiped her face with both hands.

Aira: "I take back three unkind things I said about her eyebrows."

Leon stared at the empty air where Senna's record had been.

Leon: "Only three?"

Aira: "I am grieving, Leon. Let me be generous in stages."

This time the almost-laughter reached more than one person.

It did not make anything better.

It made the room less impossible to breathe in.

---

Noctis had answered at noon, initially without Lucien.

The official notice arrived in black script with a pale border.

**NOCTIS DOMINION COLLEGE REQUESTS RETURN OF STUDENT REMAINS**

**SUBJECT: CAEL NOX**

**STATUS: NOCTIS ENROLLED CONDUIT SUPPORT**

The Black Circle snapped into focus.

Every rune lit at once. The chamber temperature dropped.

Several healers stepped back before they could stop themselves.

I did not blame them.

My first thought was uncontrolled: I could erase not the notice, but the idea behind it.

The whole old grammar that kept finding new ways to call a dead boy useful.

Elira's hand slid over mine. Her palm was cold.

Elira: "Haru." One word again.

My name was doing too much work today. I breathed in.

The cold metal taste behind my sternum sharpened. I breathed out. The notice remained. So did I. Rhea stood.

The red seal over Cael brightened until it cast clean light across the stone.

President Valmont: "Request denied."

Her answer wrote itself beneath the Noctis notice without delay or committee language.

**AURELIS ANSWER: DENIED**

**CAEL NOX IS RECORDED AS PROTECTED WITNESS OF AURELIS**

**FINAL PUBLIC AMENDMENT: HIS CHOICE IS NOT RETURNABLE PROPERTY**

Rhea looked at Nera and Oric.

President Valmont: "Do either of you contest the wording?"

Nera's face had gone very still.

Nera: "No." Oric's throat moved.

Oric: "No."

Rhea looked at me next, not for permission but warning.

President Valmont: "Haru?" I looked at Cael.

At the flowers by his feet.

At Leon's hands, still curled as if they remembered holding weight.

At Elira breathing beside me because Cael no longer did.

Haru: "Leave the notice visible." Aira turned toward me. So did Halden.

Haru: "If they asked for him like that, people should see it."

The Black Circle slowed, directed rather than soothed.

Rhea's expression shifted by a fraction.

President Valmont: "Agreed."

She archived the request in the public record.

Mira copied it three times.

The third copy tore where her pencil pressed too hard.

Finn taped the tear with a strip from his own notebook.

That small act nearly undid me, perhaps because it was the opposite of resurrection: no ancient doctrine or celestial ring, ju.

---

We learned about Noctis' internal fracture through a leak before we learned through official channels. That felt appropriate.

Noctis official channels had spent too long polishing cruelty until it reflected authority.

The leaked relay carried no image, only audio and a transcript that flickered as if someone had copied it in a hurry.

Darian Thorne's name appeared at the top.

**STATUS: HOUSE RESTRICTION**

**DISCIPLINARY HOLD PENDING COUNCIL REVIEW**

Nera inhaled sharply.

Oric closed one hand around the other wrist.

The audio began halfway through a sentence.

Darian Thorne: "-then charge me with disloyalty in a public room. Do not do it behind a sealed door and pretend the students cannot hear cowardice through stone." A second voice answered.

Noctis Councilor: "You assisted Aurelis in obstructing a sanctioned reclamation proceeding."

Darian Thorne: "I assisted a child in saying no."

Noctis Councilor: "Cael Nox was not a child in the legal sense."

Darian Thorne: "How convenient for everyone who used him like one."

The transcript trembled, then recovered. Another voice entered. Lucien.

Lucien: "You are enjoying moral clarity now that the cost has already been paid by someone else."

Darian Thorne: "And you are still trying to sound above a grave." Silence.

Even through damaged audio, it had shape.

Lucien: "Cael made himself proof."

Nera's fingers dug into the black cloth at her knee.

Darian Thorne: "No. That is the part you cannot bear. He made himself unavailable to your proof." The audio cracked.

Lucien: "The Black Circle exists. The world cannot unsee it."

Darian Thorne: "The world also saw why it appeared."

Noctis Councilor: "Enough."

Darian Thorne: "No. Not enough. That has been the problem." The leak ended.

No one moved for several seconds. Then Oric whispered:

Oric: "He will be punished for that."

Nera's voice came out rough.

Nera: "He knew."

I thought of Cael warning us that Lucien had patience.

I thought of Darian speaking too late and still speaking.

I thought of how many people were learning that courage after failure still mattered, even when it could not raise the dead. Elira looked at Nera.

Elira: "We preserve the transcript." Nera nodded.

Nera: "And we answer it." Aira blinked.

Aira: "Now?" Nera looked toward Cael.

Nera: "Now."

She stood slowly, every movement precise because if she moved carelessly she might fall apart.

Then she faced the public record.

Nera: "Darian Thorne did not save Cael Nox in time. Neither did I. Neither did Oric Sen. That failure is part of the record." Oric flinched. Nera kept going.

Nera's voice remained steady, fingers resting on the table. "But late witness is not worthless witness. Noctis teaches that failure cancels testimony. That is a.

Oric: "We reject that doctrine." The Foundation pool answered.

**DOCTRINE CHALLENGE RECORDED**

Cael did not move.

Of course he did not. The sentence mattered anyway.

---

Outside the chamber, Aurelis became a city trying to lower its voice around a wound.

We did not see most of it directly. We heard pieces.

Healers moving in pairs because no one wanted to be alone in the old corridors.

Students gathering in stairwells instead of classrooms, whispering Black Circle in tones that made the words either prayer or panic.

Faculty arguing over whether lessons were suspended or whether normalcy itself was a protective measure.

Notice crystals turning black and silver, then gold, then back again as old systems and current administration fought politely over design priority.

At some point near midafternoon, a message from Drakenshard arrived carved in heavy red-gold script.

Mara Kest's seal burned at the bottom.

Rhea read it aloud because the wording was too blunt to be mishandled by summary.

President Valmont: "Drakenshard Martial Academy acknowledges the courage of Cael Nox, the restraint of Haru Aerlen, and the dishonor of doctrines that force students to become weapons against their own consent." Cassian stopped moving stone.

President Valmont: "We do not fear power. We fear cruelty wearing rank. Drakenshard will not support containment of the Black Circle bearer without evidence of hostile action. We will support investigation of Noctis practices with full witness access." Aira stared.

Aira: "That is the politest punch I have ever heard." Cassian's mouth twitched.

Cassian: "Drakenshard punches in complete sentences."

The Valemere message followed ten minutes later.

Soren Ashvale appeared this time, not as a formal council recording but as a live relay. He stood in a Valemere medical hall. Behind him,.

He also looked like someone who had insisted on being present.

Soren bypassed Rhea and me and bowed first to Cael.

Soren: "Valemere Royal Institute records Cael Nox as a witness whose final act confirmed a pattern of Noctis harm previously denied in Talen Mire's case."

Talen lifted his braced hand.

Talen: "I did not know him." His voice was soft.

The whole chamber leaned toward it without moving.

Talen: "But I know what it means when your pain is called procedure. I know what it means when adults tell your family that naming cruelty will ruin your future more than surviving it already did." He swallowed.

Talen: "Cael Nox should be alive. I am grateful. I am angry. Both are true." Elira bowed her head. Talen looked at her.

Talen: "Elira. I am glad you are alive."

Elira's hand tightened around mine.

Elira: "I am sorry for the cost."

Talen's eyes shifted to Cael.

Talen: "So am I."

The relay dimmed, but Soren spoke once more.

Soren: "Valemere will attend the funeral if permitted." Rhea answered immediately.

President Valmont: "Permitted."

Then she added, because Rhea Valmont understood power as placement:

President Valmont: "Witness seating will be public." Soren's expression changed. Respect, I thought. And grief.

Soren: "Understood." The relay closed. Elira's shoulders sagged.

Professor Valen reached for her again.

Elira: "I know."

Professor Valen: "Do you?"

Elira looked annoyed for half a second, and the relief of seeing any ordinary expression on her face almost hurt.

Elira: "No."

Professor Valen: "Good. Then let us begin with honesty. You need rest before sunset." Elira looked at Cael. Professor Valen's voice softened.

Professor Valen: "Rest here if you must. But rest." Aira was already moving.

She took command of two council aides, three blankets, one privacy screen, and a heated basin with the exhausted fury of a person who had decided logistics could stand in for screaming.

Aira: "Fine. We are making a medical corner. Nobody gets symbolic about it. Elira can mourn lying down." Elira did not argue.

That frightened me more than some of the magic had.

---

I thought the Black Circle would fade when Elira slept. It did not.

It dimmed, but it remained behind me, turning with patient inevitability.

The old record-echo appeared while the chamber was at its quietest.

Liora Aerlen-Valen did not arrive with ceremony.

One moment there was only dust, broken stone, and the sound of Elira's shallow sleeping breaths from behind the privacy screen.

The next, a woman made of amber record-light stood near the pool with her hands folded at her waist. Halden saw her first. Of course he did. His pen stopped moving.

Professor Halden: "Record echo."

Liora's gaze moved from him to Rhea, then to Professor Valen, then to me.

Liora: "Not record only."

Professor Valen's face went still in a way I could not read. Liora looked at Cael.

When she spoke again, her voice lowered.

Liora: "The dead should not need to become architecture." The Black Circle shifted. It recognized her.

Or recognized the old language in her.

Liora stepped closer to the edge of its pressure.

Liora: "You are waiting for a decision."

I knew she meant the circle.

I also knew she meant me.

Haru: "I do not know what decision."

Liora: "Wall or witness."

Aira looked over from the medical corner, eyes sharp despite exhaustion.

Liora: "The Black Circle can close around grief and become a wall no one can reach through. Many will encourage that. Some through fear. Some through worship. Some because walls are easier to administer than wounded people." Rhea's mouth tightened.

Liora: "Or it can remain answerable to witnesses."

Haru: "Answerable is dangerous."

Liora: "So is unanswerable." The words were simple.

They entered the room like a key entering an old lock. I looked at Cael.

**ALLEGATIONS: INSTITUTIONAL ABUSE / COERCIVE DOCTRINE / WITNESS SUPPRESSION / UNLAWFUL CONDUIT CONDITIONING**

A Noctis official stepped forward.

Noctis Official: "The Council has heard only contaminated testimony gathered under an extra-classification event."

Senna turned the relay toward Cael's bier.

Magistra Voss: "State your name and office before you call a dead student's testimony contamination."

The official looked at the flowers, the severed binding rings, and the Noctis students waiting without delegation permission.

He did not state either.

Senna let his silence enter the record.

Then the next measures wrote themselves above the fountain instead of coming from her mouth.

**FINAL CONDUIT CLAUSES: EMERGENCY SUSPENSION ACROSS MEMBER SCHOOLS**

**DOMINION SEVERANCE: EMERGENCY PROHIBITION PENDING INVESTIGATION AND RATIFICATION**

**ACTIVE MATERIAL, TRAINING RECORDS, AND INSTRUCTIONAL ROUTES: PRESERVE FOR REVIEW**

Nera folded over one breath. Oric caught her elbow and released it as soon as she was steady. Neither of them looked relieved. Suspension had arrived after Cael, which meant relief came with teeth.

The Noctis official found his voice.

Noctis Official: "You are suspending accredited curriculum on the word of defectors." Senna's burned hand closed.

Magistra Voss: "No. I am suspending a fatal route after its activation was witnessed across every relay your institution demanded." Her voice remained exact.

That made the anger inside it harder to dismiss.

A second crystal lit beside the first.

**INTERIM WITNESS-PROTECTION DIRECTIVE**

**CHOSEN PRESENCE MAY NOT BE REMOVED EXCEPT BY DIRECT, WITNESSED, TIME-LIMITED MEDICAL NECESSITY**

**INSTITUTIONAL CONVENIENCE IS NOT MEDICAL NECESSITY**

**CAEL NOX: PROTECTED WITNESS / PUBLIC SEQUENCE PRESERVED**

A sound moved through the courtyard. Not cheering.

Cael's name had been made official too late for him to hear it. No one there was cruel enough to confuse recognition with repair.

Elira's fingers tightened around mine.

Senna looked at the bier before continuing.

Magistra Voss: "His final act exposed a system that trained him to mistake being spent for being valued. The record will preserve his choice. It will also preserve the coercion that narrowed it. Any summary that removes either will be challenged by my office."

Nera made a broken sound behind her hand.

The public crystals changed again.

This time the script hesitated.

**EXTRA-CLASSIFICATION EVENT: CONFIRMED**

**ATTACHED WITNESS: HARU AERLEN, AURELIS STUDENT**

**PROPOSED TERM: BLACK CIRCLE / CLASSIFICATION UNRATIFIED**

There it was.

Not my name beside a settled rank. My name beside an argument powerful people had not yet finished trying to own.

A red-black minority seal struck across the notice before Senna could speak.

**EMERGENCY MOTION ? PROVISIONAL CONTAINMENT OF HARU AERLEN**

The courtyard chilled. Aira stopped writing. Rhea's seal rose.

Senna reached the crystal first. She pressed her burned palm against Krail's motion. White light cut through the old wound, and her fingers shook once. Only once.

Magistra Voss: "Entered into public record." The word **ENTERED** appeared.

Then she drew one line through **CONTAINMENT**.

Magistra Voss: "Denied in immediate form."

Somewhere beyond the relay, people began shouting.

Senna did not raise her voice to compete.

Magistra Voss: "I will not authorize removal of a student from every person who can name what happens to him and call the isolation caution."

The line through the motion brightened.

Magistra Voss's voice remained steady, fingers resting on the table. "No containment. No elimination order. No compulsory demonstration. No isolated classification panel. Any stability review must include.

Rhea stepped beside the relay.

President Valmont: "Aurelis objects to every future motion that begins by removing the student from his own record."

Magistra Voss: "Recorded."

The denial did not become freedom. Krail's seal remained visible beneath the line, proof that the motion could return wearing revised language.

I preferred seeing the knife.

One final notice opened over the fountain.

**INTER-NATIONAL SCHOOLS TOURNAMENT: SUSPENDED PENDING INVESTIGATION**

**OPENING-BLOCK RESULTS: ARCHIVED AS SEQUENCE / NOT FINAL STANDING**

**RESUMPTION OR RECONSTITUTION: SUBJECT TO STUDENT-HARM REVIEW**

Valemere's witness seal lit in agreement. Drakenshard accepted with grim silence. The Noctis delegation looked toward its banners as if someone had cut the ropes but left the cloth hanging.

The tournament had not resolved. Neither had the investigation.

For the first time that evening, the law looked less like an ending than a battlefield honest enough to admit where its lines were.

Magistra Voss: "Haru Aerlen, do you understand the interim terms?"

The Black Circle pressed beneath my skin.

Everyone waited for the myth to answer.

I made the student answer first.

Haru: "Yes." My breath steadied against the cold air.

Magistra Voss: "Do you accept stability review under distributed witness protocol?" I looked at Elira.

She looked exhausted, furious, alive.

She nodded once, standing with me while I decided rather than deciding for me. I looked at Aira.

She mouthed, very clearly, Do not say anything ancient.

That helped more than it should have. I looked at Cael. At the flowers. At the rings. At the witness pages.

Haru: "I accept review."

I let the next words come slowly.

Haru: "I do not accept ownership."

The fountain water turned black and silver for one heartbeat. Then clear again. Senna bowed her head.

Magistra Voss: "Recorded."

Neither Noctis nor Aurelis applauded. This was not victory. Cael was still dead.

Justice would have been him rolling his eyes at Aira's naming conventions from the back of a crowded room.

Justice would have been Nera apologizing to him while he was alive to decide what to do with it.

Justice would have been Elira never learning what absence felt like from the inside.

It was not justice, but it was the beginning of consequences.

Sometimes beginnings arrived late and limping.

We still had to meet them.

---

Haru: "I did not prepare remarks."

It was a terrible opening. Aira's face confirmed it.

She stood near the front with both hands clasped so tightly that her knuckles had gone pale, and even through grief I could see.

I stood at the fountain's edge with Cael before me and the whole world too close.

The Black Circle remained hidden.

Everyone knew it was there.

That made hiding feel less like a lie and more like restraint.

Haru: "I tried to write something. Everything sounded like I was making his death useful." My voice roughened. I let it.

Haru: "Cael had enough of that." Leon looked down. Cassian's jaw worked once.

Haru: "He saved my life twice." The words surprised people. I felt the shift.

Haru: "The first time, he came to us with proof when Noctis wanted him afraid. He warned us. He testified. He let people stand near him even though closeness had been dangerous for most of his life."

Nera pressed a hand over her mouth.

Haru: "The second time..." I looked at Elira. She was crying. Not hiding it.

Haru: "The second time, he brought Elira back."

The Black Circle flickered beneath my shirt.

I placed one hand over it. Not to hide. To acknowledge.

Haru: "When she died, I lost the first moment. The Black Circle opened before I could choose what shape grief should have."

The courtyard did not move.

Haru: "Cael stopped me from becoming only that moment." My hand shook. I kept speaking.

Haru: "Not by restraining me. Not by obeying me. Not by becoming proof for me."

Lucien's old phrase tried to enter the air.

I did not let it.

Haru: "By choosing mercy when domination had used him, when obedience had hurt him, when every doctrine around him had tried to make his life available to someone else's need." I looked at Cael.

Haru: "He chose."

The fountain answered with a soft silver pulse.

Haru: "I do not know how to be worth that choice." Aira's eyes filled.

Haru: "I only know what I can choose next."

I turned enough to see the Noctis students at the back.

Then the Green Circle witnesses. Then Elira.

Haru: "I can choose not to make his death a command for anyone else to sacrifice themselves. I can choose not to turn power into a wall because I am afraid of losing people. I can choose witnesses even when being witnessed is uncomfortable. I can choose to remember that the strongest thing Cael did was not die." My voice almost failed.

Haru: "It was say no long enough to make one final yes his own." Elira covered her mouth. Leon bowed his head.

Haru: "Cael Nox was not proof that mercy needs victims."

I looked at the public record crystals.

Haru: "Record that." Mira did.

So did four hundred and twelve students. So did the Foundation.

**PUBLIC RECORD AMENDMENT ACCEPTED**

The Black Circle pulsed once. Small. Contained. Witnessed.

---

After the ceremony, Rhea brought us Cael's personal effects.

There were not many, which was the small box's first cruelty: a spare uniform clasp, a broken Noctis calibration bead, a frayed stri.

Nera made a sound when she saw it. Oric looked away.

Elira reached for the notebook, then stopped.

Elira: "May I?"

Nera answered because someone from Noctis needed to say the obvious truth correctly.

Nera: "He would want you to." Elira opened it.

The first page held a list in Cael's careful handwriting.

The letters were small, as if he had been conserving paper or permission. Elira read aloud.

Elira: "Things I choose." Her voice trembled.

Elira: "To be called by my name, not my role."

Nera bent forward like the words had struck her.

Elira: "To say no." Oric covered his eyes.

Elira: "To have friends, if they will have me."

Aira made a broken sound. Leon turned away.

Cassian put a hand on his shoulder and left it there.

Elira: "To matter when I am not useful." She stopped.

No one asked her to continue. She did anyway.

The last page had been written recently. The ink was darker. Pressed harder.

Elira: "If this ever becomes evidence, tell them I was afraid."

That undid something in the circle around us. Not the Black Circle. Us. Elira's voice broke.

Elira: "Tell them I was afraid, and I chose anyway. Do not let them make courage sound clean."

She closed the notebook against her chest.

For a moment, no one moved.

Then Aira took one step forward.

Aira: "We should copy it." Her voice was wrecked. Practical anyway.

Aira: "Not all of it. Not the private pages unless... unless we decide. But those lines. The first and last. They need to outlive everybody's speeches." Rhea nodded.

President Valmont: "With witness consent."

Elira looked at Nera and Oric.

Nera wiped her face with the heel of her hand.

Nera: "Yes." Her tone was clipped and precise.

Oric: "Yes." He gripped the wooden rail with both hands. Leon looked at me.

Leon: "You keep it." I stared at him.

Haru: "Why?" His face twisted.

Leon: "Because I held him after. If I keep it, I will never put it down."

The honesty cost him, and he paid it anyway.

Cassian's hand tightened on his shoulder.

Elira looked at me, asking rather than commanding. I took the notebook.

Its near-weightlessness was also unfair.

Haru: "I will keep it with witnesses." Aira nodded immediately.

Aira: "Good answer." Elira's eyes softened.

Elira: "Human answer."

The Black Circle stayed quiet.

For once, that felt like agreement.

---

Long after the crowds dispersed, the core witnesses remained by the fountain: Haru, Elira, Aira, Leon, Cassian, Nera, Oric, Rhea, Professor Valen, Halden, Mira, Finn, Soren, Talen, and Senna. Too many for privacy.

Too few for the size of the absence.

Cael's body had been moved under witness guard to the eastern hall for preparation. The flowers remained around the fountain because no one had the heart to decide which ones should go with him and which ones should become public memorial.

So Rhea decided none would be moved until morning.

Sometimes authority was useful because grief could not choose table arrangements.

The Noctis banner remained at the fountain's edge. Cut in half.

That had been Mara Kest.

She had asked permission first.

Rhea had granted it after a five-second legal review conducted entirely through eyebrow movement.

Now one half of the banner lay beside the official record as evidence of attempted claim.

The other half had been folded beneath the nightglass flowers as proof that even Noctis cloth could be made to hold witness instead of ownership.

Aira sat on the fountain rim and looked at the water.

Aira: "He should be here."

No one corrected the sentence's uselessness; that was its purpose.

Leon sat on the ground with his arms over his knees.

Leon: "Yes." His jaw set as he shifted his weight forward.

Cassian lowered himself beside him.

Cassian: "He would hate how many people talked about him."

Nera gave a small, wet laugh.

Nera: "He would stand behind someone taller." Leon looked up.

Leon: "Me."

Aira: "Obviously you. You are structurally useful."

Leon almost smiled, then did not. That was all right.

Nera looked at the fountain.

Nera: "He used to ask questions after Lucien left rooms." Oric nodded.

Oric: "Never during."

Nera: "No. Never during."

She touched the edge of the stone.

Nera: "The first question he asked me that was not about orders was whether Aurelis students got to choose their electives." Aira's face crumpled.

Aira: "That is a horrible anecdote."

Nera: "I know."

Aira: "Tell another." Nera thought. Her voice softened.

Nera: "He liked cinnamon bread." Oric looked startled.

Nera: "He pretended not to because Noctis dining monitors marked sugar preference as indulgence if you took it too often." Elira closed her eyes.

Elira: "Then we add cinnamon bread to the memorial table."

Rhea immediately made a note without debate or symbolic committee: cinnamon bread for Cael.

That almost broke us more than the speeches had.

Talen spoke from beside Soren.

Talen: "At Valemere, after injury hearings, they serve bitter tea because they think sweetness makes testimony less dignified." Mira looked offended.

Mira: "That is ridiculous."

Talen: "Yes." He adjusted the leather strap binding his casting hand.

He looked at the fountain.

Talen: "I would like cinnamon bread too, if that is permitted." Aira pointed at Rhea.

Aira: "Put him down for bread." Rhea wrote it.

Senna watched all of this with an expression I could not name.

Maybe because council reports did not usually include bread as evidence that a dead student had been a person. Maybe they should have.

Halden stood slightly apart, arms folded. Mira noticed.

Mira: "Professor?" He looked at her.

Mira: "Did Cael ever ask you anything?"

Halden's expression changed by a degree.

Professor Halden: "Once." Everyone looked at him. He clearly regretted answering. Too late.

Professor Halden: "After the formal review, he asked whether old systems could tell the difference between a conduit and a witness." Nera's face tightened.

Professor Halden: "I told him systems could be taught. People were harder."

Aira: "That is bleak."

Professor Halden: "It was accurate."

Professor Valen looked at him. Professor Halden's jaw shifted.

Professor Halden: "He said, 'Then I hope the system learns first.'" The fountain water rippled.

No one spoke for a while.

Then Mira wrote it down. Of course she did.

---

Near midnight, after Professor Valen finally threatened Elira with supervised carrying if she refused to sleep, I returned to the fountain almost alone. Aurelis had learned better.

Leon was on the western steps pretending not to guard me.

Cassian was on the east path doing the same thing with more style.

Aira had left a note on the fountain rim that read:

**DRINK WATER OR I WILL BECOME A PROCEDURAL PROBLEM.**

I drank the water beside it.

The Black Circle pulsed beneath my shirt, small and steady, no longer pretending the world did not know.

I opened Cael's notebook to the first page again. Things I choose.

The handwriting was careful enough to hurt.

I did not turn to the last page yet.

The fountain reflected the moon, the flowers, the cut banner, and my face.

For one second, the reflection behind me showed the Black Circle in full. Deep black. Silver rings.

Constellation runes moving in opposite directions with impossible order. Then the reflection changed.

Cael stood beside me in the water-not truly a ghost, perhaps memory, Foundation residue, or grief making images out of moonlight.

He looked as he had before the final stage, tired and too young and still trying to make himself smaller than the room required.

Cael: "You look terrible." I closed my eyes.

Haru: "That sounds like something Aira would invent to make me sleep."

Cael: "Probably."

When I opened my eyes, the reflection was only water again.

I did not know whether I had imagined it.

I decided not to ask the Foundation.

Some things did not need to become records immediately.

Elira's voice came from behind me.

Elira: "You left the medical room." I turned.

She stood in a robe over her uniform, hair loose over one shoulder, Professor Valen's medical seal glowing faintly at her wrist.

Behind her, at a respectful distance, Professor Valen looked deeply irritated and entirely unsurprised.

Haru: "You followed."

Elira: "Slowly. With supervision. Everyone wins."

Professor Valen: "That is not my summary."

Elira ignored that with the confidence of a patient who had chosen selective hearing as a survival tactic.

She sat beside me on the fountain rim, not too close at first and then closer. Her shoulder touched mine.

Elira: "What happens now?"

I looked at the flowers. The witness pages.

Professor Valen remained behind us, close enough to intervene and far enough to let the question belong to us first.

Then she said my name in the quieter voice she used when history had stopped being an archive and become a person sitting before her, not Professor Valen's formal witness voice.

Professor Valen: "There is one record I owe you before the Council starts asking for every other one." I turned.

She folded her hands over the medical case at her side.

Professor Valen: "When your transfer file reached Aurelis, Student Affairs nearly rejected it at ranking review. A Green Circle applicant from Lumeris District with ancient-script scores above several faculty candidates looked either impossible or inconvenient."

The fountain sounded louder for a moment.

Instructor Selene's voice returned from my first morning.

Someone argued strongly in your favor.

Haru: "It was you."

Professor Valen: "I argued that a student should not be punished because his examination answers made adults uncomfortable."

Halden, from the western steps, gave a dry sound.

Professor Halden: "That is a selective summary."

Professor Valen did not look away from me.

Professor Valen: "I also argued that anyone who could translate pre-standardization mercy clauses without being taught them deserved a room with better questions than the entrance board was asking."

My hands had gone still around Cael's notebook.

Haru: "Did you know?"

Professor Valen: "No."

She answered too quickly for comfort and too honestly to doubt.

Professor Valen: "I suspected old knowledge had touched your life somehow. I did not know the name. I did not know the danger. I certainly did not know I was helping bring the Black Circle into my own school."

Aira, from the fountain rim, wiped one eye with her sleeve.

Aira: "For the record, that is the least villainous secret admission sponsorship I have heard today." Professor Valen's mouth softened.

Professor Valen: "High praise."

I looked back at the water.

At the place where Cael's reflection had been.

Haru: "Why tell me now?"

Professor Valen: "Because people will try to make your arrival sound like a plot. Some will say Aurelis hid you. Some will say I recruited a weapon. Some will say your place here was evidence of conspiracy."

She drew a careful breath.

Professor Valen: "The first true answer is smaller. I saw a student being underestimated by a system that mistook rank for proof, and I objected. If the rest becomes more complicated, let the simple part stay in the record." Elira's hand found mine.

This time, I let the contact steady me before I had decided whether I deserved it.

Haru: "Thank you."

Professor Valen: "Do not thank me too much. I also failed to ask enough follow-up questions."

Halden: "We all did."

No one argued, and that too became part of the night. The half-banner.

The notebook in my hands.

Haru: "Noctis investigation. Council reviews. People afraid of me. People wanting to use me. People saying Black Circle like they know what it means."

Elira: "Yes." Her fingers rested lightly against the stone rail.

Haru: "Lucien is not done."

Elira: "No."

Haru: "You need to heal."

Elira: "Also yes."

Haru: "I do not know how to keep going without making Cael's death into the center of every choice."

Elira was quiet for a moment.

Then she took the notebook from my hands, closed it gently, and placed it between us.

Elira: "Maybe we do not make his death the center."

She looked at the fountain.

Elira: "Maybe we make his choices part of ours."

The Black Circle warmed once beneath my shirt-not heat or exactly comfort, but recognition.

Elira: "He chose to be called by his name."

Haru: "Cael."

Elira: "He chose to say no."

Haru: "Then we make room for no."

Elira: "He chose to have friends." My throat tightened.

Haru: "Then we stay close." Elira's hand found mine.

Elira: "He chose to matter when he was not useful."

The fountain water moved around the reflection of the moon.

Haru: "Then we stop asking people to earn care." Elira leaned against me.

This time with more weight. Still not enough. More.

Elira: "There. That is how."

I closed my fingers around hers.

The Black Circle pulsed once beneath my shirt as neither threat nor secret, only reminder.

Power without purpose had almost become destruction.

Power with witnesses, grief, choice, and mercy was not safe.

Nothing worth protecting was ever entirely safe. But it was answerable. Cael Nox was gone. The world had changed. Noctis was fractured.

The Black Circle was known.

Elira was alive beside me, breathing unevenly but breathing.

And for the first time since the Wounded City broke open, the future did not feel like a verdict already written.

It felt like a page. Heavy. Unfair. Waiting.

Together, we stayed by the fountain until the moon moved past the tower and the flowers turned silver in the dark.

## Coda: Empty Chair

No one removed Cael's chair that night.

Practical reasons existed. The room was crowded. Evidence still needed sealing. Healers were moving too fast to care about furniture. But by midnight,.

Leon sat on the floor beside it instead. Not in it. Beside.

Cassian came with two cups of tea and gave one to the empty chair before correcting himself with a curse so quiet it hurt more than if.

Haru stood at the window with Elira's hand in his, both of them alive in ways that felt too expensive.

At dawn, Mira taped a note to the chair.

Reserved does not mean owned.

No one knew whether it was for Cael, for the witness record, or for everyone who had survived him.

No one removed that either.

===== EPISODE 15 =====

# Episode 15: **The Room Where She Woke Twice**

The morning after Cael's funeral, Elira woke with both hands at her throat. Not gently.

Like someone trying to prove the path into her body had closed. I was already awake.

That was the first thing I hated about myself that morning.

Sleep would come badly for a while, if it came at all. What I hated was the part of me that had begun treating Elira's breathing as a duty. Count the inhale. Count the pause. Count the exhale. Watch the pulse at her wrist. Watch the crystal for coldness. Watch the windows. Watch the door.

Watch everything except the person beside me. Elira's eyes opened.

For one second, they were empty of the room. Then they found me.

Elira: "Haru?"

Her voice was too small.

The Black Circle stirred beneath my skin so sharply that the ward-stone under the bed frame clicked.

I pressed my palm flat against the blanket.

Haru: "I'm here."

Elira turned her head toward the ceiling. Her lips parted once. No sound came out. The dark crystal pendant rested against the white collar of her healing gown, ordinary as a raindrop, terrible as a verdict.

Elira: "I dreamed I was still in the cut."

I did not ask which cut.

There was only one that mattered.

Elira: "Everyone was calling my name from the other side, but I could not tell if they wanted me alive or useful." My hand curled. She saw it.

Elira: "Do not become angry before you hear me."

I forced my fingers open one at a time.

Haru: "I'm listening."

Elira looked at me then. Really looked. Not at the shadow under my eyes, not at the Black Circle pressure I was failing to hide, not at the room full of quiet medical sigils. At me.

Elira: "When I woke after Cael restored me, everyone was relieved."

Haru: "They love you."

Elira: "Yes." Her fingers rested lightly against the stone rail. Her eyes shone.

Elira: "And I am grateful. I am. But relief is heavy when someone else bought it."

The room's background sound dropped away.

Outside the recovery ward, morning bells rang across Aurelis. They sounded careful now. Even bronze had learned restraint.

Elira: "I keep thinking I have to make being alive worth what happened."

Haru: "You don't."

The answer came too quickly. Elira's face tightened.

Elira: "That was the correct answer."

I understood the wound in her tone before she explained it.

Correct was not the same as present.

Haru: "I'm sorry."

Elira: "For what?"

Haru: "Answering the fear instead of staying with you in it." Her expression changed. Only slightly. Enough.

I shifted closer on the narrow chair beside her bed. The healers had offered me a cot. I had refused because the chair put me between Elira and the door. Elira had noticed. Of course she had.

Elira: "You slept there?"

Haru: "No."

Elira: "That was not my question."

Haru: "Yes." My breath steadied against the cold air. She closed her eyes.

For a terrible moment, I thought I had failed her again.

Then she lifted one hand from the pendant and held it toward me. I stared at it.

Elira: "Haru."

Haru: "If I touch you while the Black Circle is unstable-"

Elira: "If you make my body into a danger zone, I will be furious." The words were weak.

The steadiness behind them was not. I took her hand. Her skin was warm.

Too warm after the memory of cold. Too fragile after the memory of stillness. Too alive for my mind to accept without wanting to guard it into a cage.

Elira's fingers threaded between mine.

Elira: "There."

Haru: "There?"

Elira: "You are allowed to want comfort too."

The Black Circle hurt beneath my ribs. Not with power. With recognition.

I bowed my head until our joined hands touched my forehead.

For a while neither of us spoke.

Senior Healer Maelin Orr entered without knocking, which I was beginning to understand was not rudeness. It was strategy. Panic hid in the pause before a knock was answered.

Maelin carried a tray with two cups, three folded reports, and the expression of a woman prepared to fight a government with a spoon if the government stood between her and a patient.

Maelin: "Good. Hands are occupied. That reduces the chance of either of you doing something dramatic."

Elira made a sound that was almost a laugh.

Maelin's gaze flicked to me.

Maelin: "Aerlen, your circle pressure cracked a bed ward."

Haru: "It clicked."

Maelin: "It clicked because it was deciding whether to crack. Do not negotiate with furniture."

Elira's fingers tightened around mine.

Elira: "He was listening."

Maelin set the tray down.

Maelin: "Then I will reward the miracle with instructions."

She unfolded the first report.

Maelin: "Elira Vale is medically alive, magically restored, politically inconvenient, and not available for public display."

Elira: "That last one sounds like a diagnosis."

Maelin: "It is the most important diagnosis." The second report opened.

Maelin: "Haru Aerlen is not medically my patient because no one has yet invented a form foolish enough to describe him."

Haru: "That seems fair."

Maelin: "He is, however, standing close enough to my patient to become part of her recovery environment. Therefore I am allowed to be unpleasant."

Elira: "She enjoys that part."

Maelin: "Correct."

The third report remained folded.

That one had Council wax.

Maelin did not touch it yet.

Maelin: "Professor Valen and Magistra Senna Voss agree on one thing, which has alarmed several committees. You both need removal from active witness pressure." The air changed.

I felt old systems listening from the walls.

Haru: "Removal sounds like separation."

Maelin: "That is why the wording has been rejected." She looked at Elira.

Maelin: "You are not being hidden. You are not being isolated. You are being placed on protected recovery leave with chosen witness access, medical oversight, and no ceremonial obligations."

Elira's thumb moved against mine.

Elira: "Where?"

Maelin unfolded the Council notice.

Maelin: "The Vale family maintains a small restoration house on the eastern lake road. It predates Circle standardization, which means it has fewer modern relay hooks for Noctis to annoy me with. Professor Valen inspected it at dawn. Rhea Valmont has already bullied three clerks into approving the security perimeter."

Haru: "Elira goes there."

Maelin looked at me over her reading glasses.

Maelin: "Try again." I stopped.

Elira did not let go of my hand.

Haru: "Elira chooses whether to go there."

Maelin: "Better."

Elira stared at the window. Morning light made her hair look almost white where it spread over the pillow.

Elira: "Would Haru be allowed to come?"

Maelin: "Allowed is a weak word. Your sleep worsens when he is outside the ward. His circle pressure worsens when he is ordered away from you. Councilor Krail dislikes this evidence, which improves my confidence in it."

For the first time that morning, Elira smiled. Small. Tired. Real.

Elira: "Then I choose to go."

Her gaze returned to me.

Elira: "With you." The Black Circle steadied.

Not because danger had passed.

Because she had spoken as if the future still belonged to choice.

By noon, Aurelis knew only the official version.

Elira Vale had entered protected recovery leave after catastrophic magical injury. Haru Aerlen, publicly recognized as the Black Circle bearer under distributed witness review, had been assigned as chosen proximity witness because separation posed greater instability than supervised closeness. Student Council retained access. Medical authority retained priority. Council review remained active, cold stone and the smell of drying ink anchoring the words.

Aira read the notice twice in the ward doorway.

Aira: "That is the least romantic love letter I have ever seen."

Elira, sitting upright with too many pillows behind her, lifted an eyebrow.

Elira: "You were expecting flowers from the Council?"

Aira: "No, but 'chosen proximity witness' is a tragic thing to call a boyfriend."

Leon stood behind her with a sealed satchel of ward maps and an expression that suggested he had been forced to carry feelings in public.

Leon: "It means he is legally allowed to stand near her."

Cassian leaned against the opposite wall.

Cassian: "Romance thrives."

I looked at all of them.

Haru: "Are you here to help?"

Aira: "Emotionally or logistically?"

Haru: "Either."

Aira: "Logistically, yes. Emotionally, we are improvising."

Rhea arrived five minutes later with Professor Valen, two council seals, and enough authority to make the hallway straighten.

Rhea: "The route is clean. Three relay points are disabled. Two are being watched. One clerk attempted to classify recovery leave as an appearance withdrawal."

Cassian: "Attempted?"

Rhea: "He has learned vocabulary."

Professor Valen came to Elira's bedside and took her hand with a gentleness that made her authority sharper, not softer.

Professor Valen: "You are not leaving the story, Elira. You are taking back the parts of it no hearing room is owed." Elira's composure cracked. Not much.

Enough that everyone looked away except me.

She wanted me to see. So I did.

Elira: "What if I do not know how?"

Professor Valen: "Then begin with small rebellions."

Elira: "Such as?" Professor Valen smiled.

Professor Valen: "Sleep because you are tired, not because healers are counting hours. Eat something because it tastes good, not because restoration requires it. Hold his hand because you want to, not because witness theory approves." Aira nodded solemnly.

Aira: "Scandalous."

Elira's laugh broke this time.

It did not last long.

But while it existed, the room remembered who she was before everyone learned how close the world had come to losing her.

The laugh also did something less poetic and more important.

It made Maelin check the chart again.

She did not smile. Senior Healer Maelin Orr seemed professionally opposed to encouraging anyone to think she had feelings before lunch, but the corner of her mouth changed by half a degree, and the ward-stone at Elira's bedside shifted from amber to a softer green.

Maelin: "Respiration steadier."

Aira pointed at Elira with grave triumph.

Aira: "Medical laughter. I will be unbearable about this."

Maelin: "You already are."

Aira placed one hand over her heart.

Aira: "Recognition from a senior healer."

Leon, who had been standing near the door with the posture of a guard trying to pretend he was furniture, muttered:

Leon: "Please do not encourage her."

Cassian: "Encouragement is not required. Aira is self-fueling."

Aira: "Thank you."

Cassian: "That was not praise."

Aira: "It was accurate, which is better."

For one fragile moment the room sounded almost like the team room after training, before Noctis filings, before public relays, before a witness died to return the girl sitting in the bed.

Then Elira's hand moved to her throat again. The motion was small. Everyone saw it.

Everyone pretended not to, except Maelin, who had no interest in pretending around symptoms.

Maelin: "Name it."

Elira's fingers stilled against the pendant.

Elira: "It feels like my body is waiting for someone to correct it."

The room lost its borrowed light carefully, as if even grief had learned to step quietly around her.

Maelin set the chart down.

Maelin: "That is not a magical symptom."

Haru: "But Dominion used magic." Maelin looked at me.

Maelin: "Do not make the mistake of thinking the wound ends where the spell ended." I closed my mouth. She was right.

I hated how often healers were right when they said things I did not know how to survive hearing.

Maelin turned back to Elira.

Maelin: "Your body remembers interruption. It will ask for proof. You may answer it with touch, breath, food, anger, tears, silence, or a professional complaint submitted to whichever cosmic authority designed nerves." Elira stared.

Maelin: "I have forms."

Aira made a sound that was almost a laugh and almost a sob. Elira's mouth trembled.

Elira: "Do you really?"

Maelin: "No. But I should."

The pendant gave one small violet pulse, not magic enough to matter to a system, only enough to make my fingers ache with wanting to fix what could not be fixed by force.

Elira saw my hand move.

She did not let me hide it.

Elira: "Haru." I looked at her.

Elira: "Sit."

It was not a request.

I sat on the chair beside the bed.

She held out her hand.

This time I did not make her ask twice. Her palm was warm.

That fact entered me with such violence that I nearly lost my breath.

Elira: "No counting." I froze.

She squeezed my hand once.

Elira: "You are doing it in your eyes." Aira looked at me.

Leon looked at the floor.

Cassian suddenly found the ceiling very interesting.

Maelin, merciless as weather, said:

Maelin: "Counting can be a bridge. It can also become a cage. Decide which one you are building before you finish the walls."

The Black Circle went still beneath my skin. Not obedient. Listening.

Haru: "I do not know how to stop."

Elira's expression softened in a way that hurt more than accusation would have.

Elira: "Then do it where I can see you. Do not turn my breathing into a private prison."

I looked at our joined hands.

Haru: "I was afraid that if I stopped watching, the world would take you again." The words were quiet.

Too quiet for the room. But everyone heard them.

Elira did not look away.

Elira: "And I was afraid that if I woke needing you, you would become only the person who watches doors."

That went through me cleanly. No blood. No visible wound.

Just the old shape of loneliness opening where I had thought power lived.

Haru: "I do not want that."

Elira: "Then stay beside me, not around me."

Maelin picked up the chart again as if the entire room had not just rearranged itself around one sentence.

Maelin: "Good. Emotional hazard named. Physical hazard next."

Ten minutes later, two council assistants brought Rhea three sealed documents. Her expression made both of them stand half a step behind her.

Rhea: "Noctis has filed an objection to protected recovery leave." Elira closed her eyes.

Leon: "They object to her recovering?"

Rhea: "They object to the leave being protected."

Cassian: "Ah. They prefer injured witnesses where they can reach them."

Rhea's silence confirmed more than a yes would have.

Something cold moved under my ribs. Old. Black.

Hungry for a clean solution.

Elira's thumb pressed against my knuckle. Not a restraint.

A reminder that my hand was holding hers.

Rhea crossed the room and placed the documents on the small table by Maelin's chart.

Rhea's voice remained steady, fingers resting on the table. "The objection is denied in immediate effect. Senna Voss logged the denial under medical authority, witness integrity, and public sequence protection. I am here because denial does not mean absence of pressure."

Maelin: "Translation: they will try to make rest look suspicious."

Rhea: "Yes." Her emergency seal rested flat on the dark wood.

Aira took out her notebook.

Aira: "Fine. We make rest boring in public and sacred in private." Everyone looked at her.

Aira: "What? That was excellent."

Professor Valen, who had remained quietly near Elira's bedside through the entire exchange, said:

Professor Valen: "It was." Elira's shoulders lowered.

She had brought a folded shawl, a small cedar box, and the tired authority of someone who had argued with the Council before breakfast and won because the alternative offended history.

Professor Valen: "The restoration house at Lake Velis is ready. Its wards predate the Circle hierarchy and do not classify visitors by rank unless they attempt harm."

Haru: "Unless?"

Professor Valen: "Old houses are allowed opinions."

Maelin: "The medical wards are mine."

Rhea: "The outer route authority is mine." Aira lifted her pen.

Aira: "The snack strategy is mine."

Leon: "Why does snack strategy require a notebook?"

Aira: "Because trauma recovery without food becomes philosophy, and philosophy makes Haru worse." I should have objected.

I could not find a lie strong enough.

Elira's fingers tightened around mine in silent laughter.

Professor Valen set the cedar box on the bed tray and opened it.

Inside was a simple strip of cloth: a black ribbon edged in silver thread, neither jewelry nor charm. Elira looked at it.

Professor Valen: "A recovery token from the house. It records voluntary presence, not condition. If you tie it to a door, the house knows the room is chosen. If you tie it to a wrist, the house knows the person has entered by consent. If you throw it into the lake, the house will judge you dramatic but respect the decision."

Elira touched the ribbon with two fingers.

Elira: "Consent first."

Professor Valen: "Always, if the old builders were having a good century."

There was humor in her voice, but not carelessness. Rhea's gaze sharpened.

Rhea: "Can Noctis subpoena the house's record?"

Professor Valen closed the box.

Professor Valen: "They may attempt to subpoena the lake if they enjoy humiliation." Cassian's smile returned.

Cassian: "I want to watch that hearing."

Maelin: "No one is watching anything for forty-eight hours except meals, medicine, sleep, and whether Haru Aerlen remembers chairs exist for sitting rather than strategic door control." I looked at her.

Maelin: "Do not test me. I have sedatives and moral clarity." Elira laughed again. Longer this time. The ward-stone turned green. No one celebrated.

Celebration would have asked too much of the moment.

But Aira wrote something down, and when I glanced at the page, I saw:

**Second laugh. Voluntary. Witnessed by friends, not systems.**

She noticed me looking and did not hide it.

Aira: "Some records are ours."

The sentence settled over the room more gently than any ward.

Rhea placed one more item on the table. Not a document.

A small square of folded black cloth, sealed with Aurelis blue and the plain white mark Senna Voss had used for protected witness material. Elira's smile faded.

Rhea: "Cael's public funeral record has been copied for the restoration house archive. Not the Council version. The Aurelis student version." No one moved.

I could hear the ward-stone in the bed frame hum once, soft as a held breath.

Elira: "Why bring it here?" Rhea's expression remained formal.

In that exact manner, she survived tenderness in public.

Rhea: "Because recovery leave is not exile from grief. And because Noctis filed a correction request at dawn."

Leon swore under his breath. Cassian's smile vanished. Aira's pen stopped.

Haru: "Correction?"

Rhea: "They object to the phrase voluntary refusal of ownership. They prefer final service under catastrophic confusion."

The Black Circle did not rise. It went colder. That was worse.

Elira's fingers tightened around mine until it hurt. Good.

Pain in my hand kept me in the room.

Elira: "No."

One quiet, wounded word, absolutely alive. Rhea inclined her head.

Rhea: "The correction was denied. Mira's gallery copy, Nera's testimony, Darian's dissent, and Iven Sahl's funeral presence all support the existing language."

Elira looked at the folded cloth.

Elira: "Iven?"

Rhea: "He asked if students from Noctis may sign the Aurelis copy without being absorbed into Noctis' official delegation."

Aira's eyes filled before she could make them sharp.

Aira: "Good."

Leon: "Is he safe?"

Rhea: "As safe as a Noctis student publicly refusing convenient language can be. Which is to say not enough. Senna Voss has opened a protected channel." Elira closed her eyes.

For a moment I thought the news would push her back under the weight of the funeral.

Instead she opened them and looked at Rhea.

Elira: "Send him my thanks."

Rhea: "As Elira Vale or as primary witness?" Elira's face tightened. Then steadied.

Elira: "As Elira."

Professor Valen's eyes softened behind her glasses.

Maelin pretended to adjust the chart.

Aira wrote the answer down.

I wanted to memorize the way Elira said her own name there, stripped of title and function, and I hated that memorizing it felt like another record.

So I did not make it sacred.

I only held her hand.

Rhea folded the cloth back into her satchel.

Rhea: "The copy will be at the house if you request it. It will not present itself otherwise." Elira breathed in.

Elira: "Thank you."

Cassian leaned against the wall, quieter than usual.

Cassian: "Cael would have hated all this paperwork." Leon looked at him.

Cassian: "What? He had taste."

For one second, grief made room for the fact that Cael had been a person who could have hated paperwork, not only a symbol around which it gathered. Elira's mouth trembled.

Elira: "He would have corrected the grammar."

Aira wiped at one eye with the back of her wrist and glared at the page as if ink had betrayed her.

Aira: "Then we will correct it for him."

When the carriage came, I helped her stand. She hated needing help.

I knew because she let me see that too.

Haru: "Tell me if I am holding too tightly."

Elira: "You are."

I loosened my grip immediately.

She did not move away.

Elira: "Better."

Maelin brought the wheeled chair herself, both hands on the handles and an expression that dared servant, council aide, or spectator to turn medical equipment into symbolism.

Elira looked at the chair.

Then at the ward entrance beyond it.

The hallway was not long.

It only felt long because every door between here and the carriage had learned how to become public.

Maelin: "You may ride."

Elira: "May?" Maelin's mouth tightened.

Maelin: "Medical permission. Not command." Elira nodded once.

Then she placed one hand on the bed rail and pushed herself upright.

Every person in the room moved without moving. Rhea's seal brightened.

Leon took half a step.

I nearly stood in front of the door.

Elira saw all of it.

Elira: "No."

The word stopped us more cleanly than a ward.

She breathed through the first wave of dizziness. Her hand shook on the bed rail. The pendant at her throat stayed dark. The room waited, badly.

Elira: "I will use the chair if I need it." Maelin studied her face.

Maelin: "You need it."

Elira: "Probably." That was not defiance.

For that exact reason, everyone listened.

Elira: "But I want to walk the first door." Aira's pen lowered.

Elira looked at me then.

Elira: "Beside me." Not around me.

She did not say the second half aloud.

She did not have to.

I stepped to her side instead of the doorway.

It took visible effort. I hated that it took effort. I was grateful she could see the effort and not have to guess where I had put the fear.

Haru: "Beside you."

Elira placed her hand on my sleeve, not my arm. Cloth again.

Choice with one layer between skin and panic.

Rhea opened the ward door.

The corridor beyond was lined with students, healers, council aides, and faculty pretending badly that they had not gathered into a farewell. The wheeled chair waited behind us like a patient argument. Elira took one step. Then another.

The hallway did not applaud. Good.

Applause would have made survival sound completed.

At the first doorframe, Elira stopped. Her breath had gone thin. Sweat stood at her temple.

Maelin moved the chair close without triumph.

Elira sat before her knees could become the room's decision.

Maelin: "Good."

Elira: "Do not sound pleased."

Maelin: "I am pleased by correct use of medical equipment. It is a private joy."

The smallest laugh moved through the room and did not break anything.

Rhea looked toward the corridor.

Rhea: "Departure terms?"

Elira's fingers tightened once on my sleeve. Then released.

Elira: "No procession." Aira wrote.

Elira: "No applause."

Mira, visible through the doorway with her sign hugged to her chest, nodded as if taking an order from someone who had earned the right to make it small.

Elira: "No one says brave."

Iven Sahl, standing beyond Mira with the Noctis students who had refused the official delegation, lifted his head.

Elira: "If anyone asks what this is, say I am leaving before I become useful to the wrong people again."

The sentence entered the hallway and did not become elegant.

For that exact reason, it held.

Rhea's council seal wrote the terms in red light beside the door.

**DEPARTURE BY STUDENT TERMS**

**NO PROCESSION**

**NO APPLAUSE**

**NO COURAGE CLAIM WITHOUT ACTOR CONSENT**

Mira copied the last line with both hands.

I thought of Elira waking with both hands at her throat.

I thought of Cael lying under Rhea's seal.

I thought of every instinct in me that wanted to make a wall between her and the watching world.

Then I walked beside the chair. Beside. Not around.

At the ward entrance, the academy had gathered despite the notice saying no public send-off. Students stood in messy rows with notebooks, flowers, ribbons, and silence. Mira Castellan held a sign that read:

**RECOVERY IS NOT ABSENCE**

Beside her, Iven Sahl stood with the Noctis students who had refused the official delegation. His hands were empty. His head was bowed. Elira saw him. Her breath caught.

Then she raised one hand in a greeting too small to become performance or speech.

Iven looked up as if someone had returned his name to him. The carriage door opened.

Elira paused before stepping inside.

Elira: "Haru."

Haru: "Yes?"

Elira: "When we get there, I do not want the first thing we do to be checking wards."

Every instinct in me objected. Every one. I swallowed them.

Haru: "What do you want first?"

She looked at the lake road beyond the academy gates, where sunlight moved through trees untouched by trial halls, witness rails, and funeral banners.

Elira: "Tea." Her fingers found mine.

Elira: "And then I want to sit somewhere no one is waiting for me to prove I survived correctly." The Black Circle quieted. Not asleep. Listening.

Haru: "Then tea first."

Elira stepped into the carriage. I followed.

Behind us, Aurelis did not cheer.

That would have been cruel.

Instead, the students stayed present as the carriage began to move. Witnesses, still.
