I put it under fear remaining.

She nodded once. No praise. Better.

The next argument was worse.

I wrote **OBSERVED INDEPENDENT ACTION** at the top of a clean page.

Mira read it upside down and frowned.

Mira: "Independent from whom?"

Elira: "From Haru."

Mira: "Then you have centered him in the category."

I hated that she was right before I finished understanding why.

She took a blank slip and wrote more slowly than Aira would have:

**ACTION NAMED BY ACTOR**

Elira: "That is less elegant."

Mira: "Yes." Her pencil pressed firmly into the rough paper.

Elira: "It is also better." Mira's mouth twitched.

The fish paperweight received another dead heading.

By the end, it looked buried under the bodies of respectable language. We kept going.

**Observed refusal** became **refusal completed before response** after Mira pointed out that witnesses were not decorations attached to decisions; the timing mattered.

**Care without debt** became **aid with exit preserved** because a Green student had written that she wanted her two-copper contribution returned if anyone used it to claim she owed Haru loyalty.

I read that line twice. Then a third time.

Elira: "She wrote that?"

Mira: "Pella. Kitchen runner. Green Circle. She said two copper is small until someone powerful decides it bought her."

The gold ring above my rejected drafts trembled once. I let it.

My first draft had protected my choice.

Mira's version protected the people who had witnessed it.

Those were not the same work.

The correction should have embarrassed me more than it did.

Instead, it made me hungry.

Not for praise. Not for victory. For the next exact shape.

I pulled the packet closer.

Elira: "Again." Mira looked up.

Elira: "Find the next place where I am making the record too elegant." That almost startled her. Then she did.

The next page came from Finn. His receipt bundle included three crossed-out totals, a notation about lamp oil, and one sentence written in the margin:

**If the Council says we were influenced, ask why influence made us keep receipts instead of hiding them.**

I laughed before I meant to.

The sound was small and rough. Mira blinked at me.

Elira: "Sorry."

Mira: "It is funny."

Elira: "It is also very Finn."

Mira: "He asked whether sarcasm could be entered as fiscal evidence."

Elira: "Can it?" Mira considered.

Mira: "If Aira labels it."

We both wrote that down.

The next dispute was over the word bravery.

I used it without thinking. Mira crossed it out.

Elira: "You dislike bravery?"

Mira: "I dislike when adults call something bravery because they do not want to admit children were scared."

There were sentences that arrived like clean bells. This one did not.

It arrived like a cup set down too hard.

Elira: "Then what word?"

Mira did not answer immediately.

She sorted three pages with her thumb. One from a Green boy who had stayed in the courtyard because his older sister was watching. One from a Blue support student who had contributed a heat charm and then asked if that meant she would be summoned. One from a Red junior who had written that Haru's presence frightened him but Krail's certainty frightened him more.

Mira: "Stayed."

Elira: "Stayed?"

Mira: "Bravery is what people call it afterward if they approve of you. Stayed is what happened."

I crossed out bravery. Wrote stayed.

The word looked plain. It held.

My wrist ached by then. The neat part of me wanted to hide it, so I set the pen down before pain could become performance. Mira saw. She did not comment.

Instead, she moved the fish paperweight onto the next stack and said, with no expression at all:

Mira: "The legal assistant recommends a break."

I looked at the painted fish.

Elira: "Does it."

Mira: "It is known for procedural mercy."

I should not have laughed again. I did.

This time the sound stayed in the room without startling me.

The break lasted seven minutes because Mira timed it.

She did not announce that she was timing it. She simply turned over the smallest hourglass from the shelf beside the desk, then pretended to be interested in the painted fish's legal prospects.

I ate half the bread.

My body accepted the food with embarrassing relief.

The room became less sharp around the edges. The lake outside returned from silver threat to water. My wrist stopped aching like a public accusation and became only a wrist again, sore because I had used it. That mattered.

A Yellow Circle prodigy was trained to treat fatigue as a scheduling problem. A Vale heir was trained to treat private weakness as something that could become public leverage if mishandled. A witness returned from death was apparently expected to become grateful enough that no one had to ask whether she was tired. I was tired.

The sentence existed without needing to become evidence.

Mira poured tea from the small pot on the side table. Badly. Half a teaspoon spilled into the saucer. Mira looked at it.

Mira: "Aira would say I have attacked the table."

Elira: "Aira would be wrong."

Mira: "Would she?" I considered the saucer.

Elira: "No."

Mira's smile appeared and vanished quickly, like a student crossing a corridor she was not sure she was allowed to use. The hourglass emptied.

Neither of us moved immediately.

That was when I understood the break had also been work.

No Council seal. No mirror. No witness form. No one asking me to prove that rest was strategic before allowing it.

Mira had made a pause and defended it by saying nothing at all.

I picked up the pen again more slowly.

Elira: "Next category."

Mira turned the hourglass back upright but did not start it.

Mira: "Next condition."

Elira: "Condition?"

Mira: "You stop before your handwriting changes." I looked down.

The last three lines slanted harder than the first.

Elira: "You noticed that?"

Mira: "You asked me to find where the record becomes too elegant. Sometimes it becomes too elegant because the person writing it is trying not to be a patient."

That one landed cleanly enough to hurt.

I set the pen down.

Then picked it up again. Not to write.

To move it to Mira's side of the desk.

Elira: "Then you write the next draft."

Mira stared at the pen as if I had handed her a weapon with unclear safety instructions.

Mira: "This is your statement."

Elira: "Yes. I will approve or reject language. You draft the witness-protection portions."

Mira: "Because I corrected you?"

Elira: "Because you are better at this part."

The words stood between us. They were not generous. They were true. Mira took the pen.

Her hand shook once before she steadied it.

I looked away in time to let her have that privately.

At midmorning, Rhea's mirror seal pulsed on the desk.

I answered before I could decide not to.

Rhea appeared in council red, hair pinned tight, expression awake in the way of someone who had not slept and had decided sleep was politically unserious.

Rhea: "Tell me you ate."

Elira: "Good morning to you too."

Rhea: "That is not food."

Mira silently lifted a plate from the side table and placed it beside my elbow. Traitor. Rhea saw.

Rhea: "Thank you, Castellan."

Mira: "I am not involved in medical enforcement."

Rhea: "Everyone says that shortly before becoming involved."

I picked up a slice of bread and took one bite with as much dignity as possible.

Rhea waited until I swallowed.

Rhea: "Senna needs your language by eleven."

Elira: "We are changing the form." Rhea's eyes sharpened.

Elira: "No named Green witness escalation. Anonymous testimony preserved unless volunteered. Categories based on observed choice, not character defense."

Rhea looked from me to Mira.

Rhea: "That is weaker in court."

Mira: "It is stronger afterward." Rhea became very still.

That was the moment I knew Mira had said the right thing.

Rhea: "Explain." Mira did.

Not loudly. Not with polish. She explained that Green students could not become permanent public evidence every time a powerful person needed protection from a better powerful person. She explained that a record which consumed its witnesses proved Krail's premise more efficiently than any Noctis argument could. She explained that anonymous testimony was not cowardice when the system had already shown it knew how to punish names. Rhea listened. I listened too.

My first draft had been elegant.

It would have harmed people.

The knowledge sat behind my ribs with the small unpleasant weight of a true thing. Rhea finally nodded.

Rhea: "Accepted. I will argue admissibility through protected student condition rather than individual credibility." Mira released a breath. Rhea looked at me.

Rhea: "Vale."

Elira: "Yes?"

Rhea: "Good correction."

It was the kind of praise that did not soften anything.

I found I preferred it. The mirror dimmed.

Mira gathered the final pages. She hesitated at the door.

Mira: "Lady Vale?"

Elira: "Elira is fine." Mira looked doubtful.

I let her keep the doubt. Names were not gifts if people had to accept them quickly.

Mira: "The note about anger. The anonymous one."

Elira: "Yes?"

Mira's thumb pressed into the paper stack.

Mira: "It was mine."

Then she left before I could answer. The door closed softly.

For a while, I stayed at the desk.

The gold ring I had made earlier had left a faint circle of warmth over the rejected pages. I touched the edge with one finger. The crossed-out lines shimmered again.

I am Elira Vale. Not enough. Still true.

I took a clean sheet and wrote the final opening.

**This record preserves student observations without converting students into instruments of my defense.**

Then:

**My choices are mine. Their witness is theirs. Neither fact authorizes ownership.**

The words were not beautiful. They worked.

At eleven, I sent the packet to Rhea and Senna under my own seal. No one stood beside me when I did it.

The room did not become less frightening because of that. It became clearer.

The seal carried my name away in gold.

For years, my name had moved through rooms before I entered them. Vale. Yellow Circle. Tournament record. Useful alliance. Public symbol. A name could become a door other people opened with their hands already full of expectations.

This time, the name left my hand attached to conditions I had chosen.

That did not make it safe.

Safe was too large a word for anything touching the Council.

But it made the danger more accurately mine.

The mirror stayed dark after the packet vanished. No immediate reply. No correction.

No praise arriving fast enough to take ownership of the act.

I sat with that silence until it stopped feeling like abandonment and began to feel like space.

Then I took Mira's anonymous note from the rejected stack and placed it beside the final copy. Not as evidence. As reminder. Angry, not enchanted. The words were inelegant.

They had saved me from writing something cleaner and worse.

When the seal left my hand, my Yellow Circle rose again.

This time I did not shape it into a ring.

I let it become seven small points of light over the desk, uneven in size, warm without symmetry. One drifted toward the window. One rested above Mira's anonymous note. One hovered over the fish paperweight as if considering a legal career. I laughed. Quietly.

The sound surprised me enough that I stopped.

Then I let myself laugh once more.

Outside, the lake held the morning in pieces of silver and gray. Somewhere downstairs, Maelin began arguing with someone about stairs. Somewhere farther away, the Council was preparing to discuss whether my nearness to another person had made me less myself. I lowered my hand.

The gold lights stayed a moment longer because I wanted them to.

Then, one by one, they went out.

I remained at the desk after the room returned to ordinary light. Not waiting. Not proving. Working.

## Coda: Seven Uneven Lights

Elira left the seven lights burning longer than necessary.

They hovered over the desk, uneven and stubborn, each one a consent line that had refused to become a leash. Old magic preferred symmetry. Councils preferred signatures. Noctis preferred obedience disguised as clarity. The lights preferred answer.

Haru watched them from the doorway. He did not ask whether she was tired. She was. He did not ask whether the vow had hurt. It had. Some questions only invited people to perform endurance.

Elira: "This one is ugly."

She pointed to the smallest light. It flickered green at the edge where gold should have held clean.

Haru: "It answered anyway." Elira looked at him.

Outside, Lake Velis moved against the shore with patient dark water. Inside, the smallest light steadied.

Elira: "Then we keep ugly answers too."

The Black Circle under Haru's skin pulsed once, quiet as agreement and nowhere near command.

===== EPISODE 19 =====

# Episode 19: **The First Hearing**

The morning after the vow did not feel like morning.

Light entered the Lake Velis bedroom in long pale bands. The lake outside was quiet enough to lie. White curtains moved in the window breeze. Somewhere in the kitchen, the old house kettle clicked once, then decided not to interrupt.

Elira slept with one hand tangled in my shirt. Not the stolen one. Mine.

The distinction mattered less than it should have.

For a while, I stayed still and let myself count nothing. Not breaths. Not pulse. Not window wards. Not the precise temperature of the pendant at her throat. The new crystal rested there, dark and calm, warm from her skin. Seven open consent lines now nested inside it instead of one closed protection route.

If Dominion tried to call her rescue an entry again, it would have to pass through questions first. Who is choosing? What is being saved?

Who is being named as cost?

Is Haru acting as protector, owner, or witness?

The last question had been Professor Valen's addition. I hated it.

I had agreed to it. That, apparently, was recovery.

Elira's fingers tightened before her eyes opened.

Haru: "I'm here."

Elira: "I know."

Her voice was rough with sleep.

Then she looked at me, really looked, and the memory of the night before passed between us without needing words. Her cheeks warmed. Mine probably did too, though I refused to provide evidence.

Elira: "You are thinking very loudly."

Haru: "I am thinking carefully."

Elira: "That is the same thing when you do it."

I looked toward the window.

She laughed softly and touched my jaw with the backs of her fingers.

Elira: "No regret."

The words struck deeper than I expected.

Haru: "No regret?"

Elira: "None."

The Black Circle did not stir. It listened.

Elira saw the relief I failed to hide. Her expression softened, then sharpened with the old Elira Vale precision that had survived death, grief, fear, and my worst instinct to become a wall.

Elira: "Do not make my certainty into something you must earn every morning." I closed my eyes.

Haru: "I will try."

Elira: "No. You will practice."

That was worse. Also better.

The mirror on the far wall chimed. Once. Neither of us moved.

It chimed again. Elira sighed.

Elira: "If that is Aira, she gets one joke before I end the call." The mirror brightened.

Magistra Senna Voss appeared instead, framed by the clean black-glass lines of an Inter-National Schools Council hearing chamber. Her silver-gray robe was fastened at the throat with a narrow white seal. Behind her, three floating transcript crystals turned slowly above an empty witness rail.

Senna: "Good morning. I apologize for the early contact."

Elira pulled the blanket higher with one hand.

I rose enough to sit between her and the mirror without blocking her. She noticed. Her eyebrow moved. I moved sideways.

Senna noticed too, because Senna noticed everything and wrote it down in polite grammar.

Senna: "The second distributed witness review has been advanced." The room lost warmth. Elira sat upright.

Elira: "Advanced by whom?"

Senna: "Councilor Krail's minority bloc filed an emergency petition during the night. The petition argues that Haru Aerlen's private proximity to you after the Black Circle manifestation constitutes unsupervised extra-classification influence over a critical witness."

I felt the old cold pressure behind my sternum. Ozone. Metal.

The house wards did not flare.

The crystal did not chill. Only me.

Haru: "They are turning recovery into contamination."

Senna: "Yes." She marked the margin with an ink flourish.

I appreciated that she did not soften it.

Elira's hand found mine under the blanket. Her grip was steady.

Elira: "And our answer?"

Senna: "Aurelis has already rejected the premise. Professor Valen, Senior Healer Orr, President Valmont, and the registered witnesses submitted a joint medical-protective objection. However, Krail has secured enough signatures to require a public preliminary session."

Elira: "When?"

Senna: "At noon."

The old house kettle clicked again in the kitchen.

This time the sound felt absurd enough that Elira almost laughed. Almost. Senna looked at me.

Senna: "Mr. Aerlen, the petition requests three immediate restrictions pending full review. First, your physical separation from Elira Vale outside supervised medical conditions. Second, a prohibition against unscheduled Black Circle manifestation. Third, compulsory demonstration of the Black Circle's limits before a Council containment panel."

The room went very quiet.

Haru: "No."

The word left me before I could make it polite.

Senna: "That is also my legal reading."

Elira's thumb moved once across my knuckles.

Elira: "He cannot demonstrate a thing designed around restraint without being pressured into exactly the failure they claim to fear."

Senna: "That is the argument I intend to preserve."

Haru: "Preserve?"

Senna's eyes narrowed slightly. Not in anger. In warning.

Senna: "Council proceedings have begun receiving external doctrine packets from institutions not named as parties. Noctis Dominion College is formally under investigation and cannot participate directly. Someone is trying to continue the argument through neutral schools, private donors, and rank-security associations." Lucien.

I did not say his name. The mirror did.

For one heartbeat, Senna's reflection fractured. Black frost drew a smile across the glass where no mouth should have been. Then the fracture vanished. Senna turned her head. Someone off-screen shouted.

The transcript crystals behind her dimmed from white to gray.

Senna: "This line is being tested. I am ending contact. Do not travel alone. Do not answer any summons not sealed by Aurelis and my office together."

Elira: "Magistra-" The mirror went dark.

For three breaths, the lake house held its silence.

Then Aira's voice came from the hallway.

Aira: "I came with breakfast and political dread."

The bedroom door opened exactly two inches.

Aira did not look inside.

Aira: "Are you both dressed enough for bread?"

Elira pressed her face into her hands.

Elira: "No."

Aira: "Terrible answer. I will leave bread outside the door like a civilized friend."

Leon: "You said you would not mention the door."

Aira: "I did not mention anything specific about the door."

Cassian: "This is the loudest discretion I have ever witnessed." Rhea's voice cut in.

Rhea: "Everyone downstairs." That did it.

Elira threw a pillow at the door.

It struck the wood with enough force to satisfy nobody.

By the time we reached the sitting room, the restoration house had stopped pretending to be peaceful.

Rhea had turned the largest table into a field office. Council notices hovered over it in separate stacks. Aira had already arranged breakfast by tactical importance: tea near Elira, bread near me, documents near herself, and one plate of honey buns in the middle as either morale or bribery.

Leon stood at the window with crossed arms, watching the road through a water-thin reflection. Cassian sat backward on a chair, outwardly relaxed, one hand near a red sigil he had carved into the air and not released. Professor Valen read Senna's last transmission with a scholar's calm and a soldier's jaw. Maelin counted Elira's pulse, then mine, then looked offended by both.

Maelin: "No fever. Elevated stress. Predictable foolishness approaching."

Haru: "The Council?"

Maelin: "You."

Elira smiled into her tea. I tried not to.

The smile lasted long enough for the room to remember it was allowed to contain something besides danger.

Then I noticed the bread in Aira's hand.

She had crushed one end of the loaf without realizing it. Flour marked the front of her uniform. The hem of her cloak was wet from the lake road, and one fastening sat in the wrong loop. Aira Solen did not misfasten clothes. She considered uneven buttons a personal accusation.

Haru: "You ran here."

Aira looked down at herself as if the evidence had betrayed her.

Aira: "I traveled with urgency and very poor terrain cooperation."

Leon did not turn from the window.

Leon: "She ran from the academy gate."

Aira: "You were not invited to improve his evidence."

Leon: "You passed me."

Aira set the wounded loaf on the table. Her fingers stayed on it.

Aira: "Senna's relay failed twice before it found Rhea. The first time, the return seal went black. The second time, it showed this house with no lights."

Her voice remained brisk. Her thumb pressed deeper into the bread.

Aira: "I knew there was probably a normal explanation. Dawn. Bad angle. No one awake because some people had finally made a medically reasonable decision."

Cassian opened his mouth. Whatever joke had arrived there saw Elira's face and changed direction.

Cassian: "I have never made a medically reasonable decision at dawn. It sounds exhausting."

Aira ignored him with less force than usual.

Aira: "I still ran. Then I bought breakfast because arriving empty-handed felt like admitting I expected a body." The room went still.

Not Council stillness. No one was waiting to turn her fear into a statement. Leon left the window and pulled out the chair beside her without looking at her. Cassian slid the honey buns closer. Rhea lowered one of the hovering documents until its blue light stopped cutting across Aira's face.

Elira reached for the crushed loaf.

Aira: "That part is structurally compromised."

Elira tore off the flattened end.

Elira: "So am I. It remains bread."

She put half on Aira's plate. Aira stared at it.

Elira: "Eat."

Aira: "I brought this breakfast."

Elira: "Then take responsibility for it."

Leon sat. That seemed to give Cassian permission to stop performing relaxation. He turned his chair around and used it correctly, though with visible resentment. Valen folded Senna's transcript. Rhea remained standing for three more seconds before Elira pointed at the empty chair beside the field-office stack.

Elira: "You too."

Rhea: "There is an active containment petition."

Elira: "It will remain active while you chew." Rhea sat.

Maelin looked pleased in the dangerous way healers looked when a patient enforced instructions on other people.

Maelin: "Miss Vale, this is the soundest judgment you have demonstrated since restoration."

Elira: "I regret giving you material."

Food moved around the table. Not elegantly. Cassian took the honey bun Aira had been avoiding and claimed it was evidence preservation. Leon poured too much tea into his own cup because he was watching the road reflection instead of the pot. Valen caught the spill with a corner of her sleeve and said nothing. Aira ate the crushed bread in small, furious bites.

I watched them and understood what the field office had hidden.

They had not come only because Krail filed a petition.

They had come because Senna's mirror had gone dark and each of them had imagined a different way we might be gone again.

Elira saw the understanding arrive. She always did.

Elira: "You can stop watching us as if blinking is jurisdictional negligence."

Leon answered before anyone could make it lighter.

Leon: "Can you promise you will still be here when I look back?"

Elira's hand stilled around her cup.

The honest answer cost her.

Elira: "No." Leon looked down.

Elira: "Neither can you. That is not permission to spend the morning rehearsing grief."

Cassian tore his bun in half.

Cassian: "What if I am naturally gifted at it?"

Elira: "Then practice something harder."

His smile came back crooked instead of bright. Good.

I had wanted to promise all of them that no relay, Councilor, doctrine, or old magic would ever take anyone from the room again. The Black Circle could have made the promise sound almost plausible.

For that exact reason, I kept it inside my teeth.

Haru: "Thank you for coming." Aira swallowed.

Aira: "Obviously."

It was not an elegant answer. It was hers.

Rhea slid a document toward me.

Rhea: "Krail's petition has three layers. The visible one is containment. The procedural one is separation. The hidden one is precedent."

I read the top line.

**Emergency Motion Regarding Extra-Classification Influence and Witness Integrity**

My false Green Circle had once been a mask.

Now every official sentence tried to make my real name into a cage.

Aira tapped the lower section.

Aira: "This is the nasty part." I read it.

The petition did not say Elira was weak.

It did not say I had harmed her.

It said proximity to an extra-classification entity after traumatic resurrection could create dependency patterns indistinguishable from consent. Every word was clean. Every word was poison.

Elira read it over my shoulder.

Her expression closed around the answer. Not frightened. Insulted.

Elira: "They are using my trauma to erase my choices."

Rhea: "Yes." Her emergency seal rested flat on the dark wood.

Elira: "Then I will answer them."

Maelin: "You will answer from a seated position after eating." Elira opened her mouth.

Maelin pointed at her with a healer's pen.

Maelin: "Miss Vale, I have now watched you die, return, nearly panic yourself unconscious in a storm, and redesign a pendant with ancient witness geometry before breakfast. If you argue with me about bread, I will sedate politics itself." Cassian looked delighted.

Cassian: "Can you do that?"

Maelin: "I am willing to attempt it." Elira took the bread.

The lake wards chimed before she finished it.

Every person at the table changed.

Leon's water reflection snapped from the road to the front gate. Cassian's unfinished red sigil closed around his knuckles. Rhea was standing before her chair had time to scrape. The Green disguise around my wrist tightened on instinct, a small lie trying to protect me from a world that had already seen through it.

Two crests waited beyond the gate seal.

Valemere silver-blue. Registered visitor marks. One Red Circle, one Blue weakened at the casting hand. Both accompanied by the paired escort lights Senna now required for travel.

Rhea read the names from the ward.

Rhea: "Soren Ashvale. Talen Mire."

Cassian let his sigil die.

Cassian: "Our most tasteful possible invasion."

The gate opened only after Rhea matched Valemere's seal to Senna's joint authorization twice. Soren stood on the other side in a plain training coat, snow melting in his dark hair. His scarred hands held a wooden box narrow enough for practice cords. Talen stood beside him with his braced hand tucked against his chest and a shallow metal bowl under his other arm. Neither carried testimony papers.

That was the first strange thing.

The second was Soren's opening sentence.

Soren: "Valemere's eleven-o'clock practice hour remains registered."

Rhea looked past him for the hidden relay, lawyer, or diplomatic trick.

Rhea: "The tournament is suspended."

Soren: "The brackets are suspended. The practice hour was not canceled."

He said it with the calm precision of someone who had spent years forcing officials to respect the difference between a rule and what they wished it meant.

Soren: "Aurelis cannot travel. We brought the hour here."

Talen shifted the bowl against his hip.

Talen: "I asked to come."

The sentence was small and ready to defend itself.

Rhea turned to him instead of Soren.

Rhea: "For practice?"

Talen: "For one hour in which no one asks me what Lucien did, what Noctis meant, or whether my hand proves a larger pattern."

His braced fingers trembled against the dark wool of his coat. He did not hide them.

Talen: "I would like to spill water badly among students."

Behind Rhea, Professor Valen's expression warmed. Maelin's did not.

Maelin: "No one here is medically cleared for heroism."

Soren: "Good. We did not bring any." Cassian leaned toward Leon.

Cassian: "I dislike him more when he is efficient."

Leon: "You dislike competition with posture."

Cassian: "I dislike posture that competes successfully."

Rhea inspected the wooden box. Four lengths of plain practice cord lay inside, each dyed Valemere blue at one end and Aurelis gray at the other. No spells. No challenge seals. No ranking tokens waiting to turn an hour into precedent.

Under them sat a folded registration card.

**SUSPENDED BRACKET PRACTICE. NO STANDING CHANGE. NO OUTPUT RECORD. NO MEDICAL INFERENCE.**

Aira read over Rhea's shoulder.

Aira: "This is the most romantic document I have seen all week."

Elira: "You saw a containment petition ten minutes ago."

Aira: "Exactly. My standards are wounded."

Talen's gaze found the honey buns on the table.

His mouth moved almost into a smile.

Talen: "Valemere served bitter tea after the memorial because sweetness was considered undignified."

Aira covered the plate protectively.

Aira: "I remember. I also remember you requested cinnamon bread with admirable courage."

Talen: "I have reconsidered. Survival may require compromise."

She handed him a honey bun.

He took it with his unbraced hand. When the paper beneath it slipped, Soren's fingers twitched toward the catch and stopped. Talen trapped the paper against the bowl with his wrist. The movement was clumsy. It was also his.

Maelin noticed all of it.

Maelin: "West garden only. Inside the visible ward line. No high-output casting. Miss Vale remains seated. Haru does not solve anything with the Black Circle. Talen stops the instant pain changes category."

Talen: "Who defines category?"

Maelin: "You. Then me if you become foolish." Talen considered that.

Talen: "Acceptable."

Elira finished the bread before Maelin could point at it again.

Elira: "Now?"

Maelin: "You are far too pleased by restrictions."

Elira: "I am pleased by practice. Restrictions are the unpleasant architecture around it."

The west garden had gone silver with morning frost. Bare rose frames divided the flagstones into narrow lanes, and the lake beyond the low wall moved in dark folds under a pale sky. Old restoration wards ran along the garden boundary, visible as soft white points when Rhea sealed the gate behind us. No Council mirrors followed. Aira checked twice.

Then a third time, because fear did not become irrational merely because it repeated.

Soren set the wooden cord box on a stone bench. Talen carried the metal bowl to the center square and lowered it carefully. Water inside shivered with the same rhythm as his braced fingers.

Talen: "Water-bind support. Three-breath hold. No movement target." Leon studied the bowl.

Leon: "That is beginner work."

Elira, already seated beneath Maelin's blanket and pretending the blanket did not exist, looked at him. Leon winced.

Leon: "I mean the structure is basic. Not that performing it is."

Leon looked like he wanted the flagstones to open. Cassian patted his shoulder.

Cassian: "An excellent start. You offended the injured guest before I did. I feel liberated."

Talen crouched beside the bowl. The brace on his casting hand was silver at the joints and dark leather across the palm, made to guide movement without pretending the damaged channels could be forced back into their old shape. He placed two fingers over the water.

A faded Blue Circle appeared at his wrist. The water rose.

Not smoothly. One side lifted first, pulling the rest into a crooked sheet. Talen's breath caught. The sheet folded, struck the rim, and sent half the bowl across the stones.

Soren caught the bowl before it tipped.

Talen recoiled as if the catch had landed on him.

Talen: "Don't." Soren released it immediately.

The bowl hit stone with a flat metal sound. More water spilled.

No one rushed to fill the silence.

Soren looked at his own hand, still shaped around the object he had stopped holding.

Soren: "I thought it would fall."

Talen: "It did."

Soren: "I could prevent damage to the bowl."

Talen: "The bowl is not learning."

Wind moved through the bare rose frames. Soren's shoulders lowered by a fraction.

Talen pressed his good hand flat to the wet stone.

Talen: "If you catch everything before I fail, we only learn what you can hold."

Talen: "Then ask whether I want the catch."

The scar across Soren's right hand went pale where he closed his fingers. He had earned it by moving too late once. The body often built doctrine faster than the mind could question it.

Soren: "Do you want me to catch the bowl?"

Talen looked at the spilled water. Then at his brace.

Talen: "Not unless it is going to hit someone."

Soren: "Understood."

There was no graceful reconciliation. Soren retrieved a cloth only after Talen nodded. Together they dried enough of the stone to keep the next attempt from becoming a different kind of lesson.

Leon paced once around the bowl.

Leon: "Your pressure drops at release, not lift."

Talen: "I know."

Leon: "Do you want an inelegant alternative?" Talen looked genuinely surprised.

Talen: "How inelegant?"

Leon: "Valemere instructors would object on aesthetic grounds."

Cassian: "Now he is seducing the room." Leon ignored him.

Elira leaned forward in her chair.

Talen made a quiet sound.

It took me a moment to understand he was laughing.

He reset his fingers over the water. Leon dismissed his demonstration ring so no one could confuse explanation with support. Talen built the shape himself: a narrow Blue line lying across the surface instead of beneath the entire volume.

The water lifted one inch. It tilted.

One edge slipped over the bowl.

Talen's shoulders jumped. His Circle flared, ready to force the mistake backward.

Elira: "Let it spill."

He looked at her, furious for half a heartbeat. Then he let it. Water struck the stone. The rest remained suspended. One breath. His braced hand shook. Two.

Soren did not catch anything.

Talen sat back on his heels, breathing as though he had run uphill.

Soren: "Again?"

Talen: "No."

The word came without apology.

Maelin: "Pain?"

No praise. No disappointment. No demand that courage repeat itself until someone else felt convinced.

Leon handed Talen a dry cloth. This time, he waited until Talen took it.

Talen: "That was very inelegant."

Talen: "Three breaths."

Leon tried not to look pleased. He failed.

For the first time that morning, the garden felt like a place students might use even if the Council did not exist.

Soren opened the wooden box.

Soren: "Good. Now the part no healer can mistake for rehabilitation."

He took the four cords from the box.

Soren: "Common-square footwork. No Circles. No channel reinforcement. One cord at the waist. Steal an opponent's without leaving the marked stones."

Cassian accepted a cord and tested its knot.

Cassian: "Can I leave the marked stones if I do it beautifully?"

Leon tied his cord at the exact regulation height.

Leon: "What constitutes leaving? Full foot or any contact beyond the line?"

Soren: "Any contact."

Cassian: "Can an opponent be encouraged beyond the line?" Soren looked at him.

Soren: "Without magic, striking, lifting, or lying about a medical emergency."

Cassian: "Your rules have become suspiciously personal."

The fourth cord waited in Soren's hand.

He held it toward me.

I had crossed tournament fields under a false Green crest, entered Foundation routes, broken a city-sized return doctrine, and watched Elira die because power had not made me quick enough to understand the trap.

A strip of cloth should not have frightened me. It did.

There was no world-ending reason to take it. No one needed protection. Refusing would not save a witness. Winning would not expose a conspiracy. Losing would injure nothing except pride, which I had spent so long treating as dangerous that I no longer knew whether I possessed an ordinary amount.

Elira watched from beneath Maelin's blanket.

She did not nod encouragement.

She knew better than to make the choice easier to blame on her. I took the cord.

Soren tied the remaining one around his own waist.

Talen stood near the square with the emptied bowl tucked under his good arm.

Talen: "I call boundaries."

Aira: "I call everything else."

Rhea: "You call nothing that enters the official record."

Aira: "Then I call with unprecedented freedom."

Elira held out her hand for Soren's score slate.

Soren gave it to her without ceremony.

Elira: "First to three points. Clean take, visible possession. If Maelin stops the round, Maelin wins."

Maelin: "Finally, a sensible competition." We entered the square.

The marked space was only twelve flagstones across. Frost remained in the seams. Bare rose frames narrowed two corners, and the low wall made the lake feel closer than it was. No crowd. No tournament banners. No ranking light waiting to turn movement into proof of bloodline. Aira raised one hand.

Aira: "Competitors ready. Dignity unprotected. Begin." Soren moved first.

Not toward any of us. Across the center, one precise step that made everyone else adjust. Leon turned to keep him in view. Cassian used Leon's turn as cover and reached for his cord. Leon slapped the hand away, offended.

Leon: "That was not honorable."

Cassian: "It was not magic, striking, lifting, or medical fraud."

Leon: "You used Soren as a visual obstruction."

Cassian: "He came that way."

Soren's fingers touched Cassian's cord.

Cassian spun, heel stopping a breath before the boundary. Talen pointed at the stone.

Talen: "Inside. Barely."

Cassian: "Barely is where legends keep their furniture."

Talen: "I can change the call if you continue speaking." Cassian looked delighted.

I had watched all three and moved nowhere.

That was the problem with having too many possible answers. My body waited for danger large enough to justify choosing one. Soren saw it.

He approached without a feint, shoulders square, hands visible. I understood the trap and still spent too much attention searching for the hidden version. His left foot cut outside mine. I stepped back. He changed direction and took Leon's cord instead.

The blue-gray strip snapped free. Elira marked the slate.

Elira: "Ashvale, one."

Leon stared at his empty waist.

Leon: "You were facing Haru."

Soren: "I was facing the square."

Cassian: "He is unbearable. I respect it deeply."

Leon retied the cord with angry precision.

The second round began faster.

Leon went directly for Cassian. Cassian retreated, laughing, and tried to pull Leon into the boundary through irritation alone. Soren angled toward me again. This time I moved before certainty arrived.

I stepped into his approach, close enough that a duelist trained for reach had to shorten his hands. His eyes changed. I reached for the cord at his right hip. He turned. My fingers caught cloth. Elira coughed behind me.

It was one cough. Dry. Small. My head turned. Soren took my cord.

The movement was so clean I felt the absence before I saw the cloth in his hand.

Elira: "Ashvale, two."

Haru: "You coughed."

Elira looked down at the score slate.

Elira: "I have lungs. They are occasionally theatrical."

Haru: "You nearly-"

The rest of the sentence carried too many graves. I stopped it.

Elira's gaze lifted to mine.

Elira: "Do not use me to make losing feel noble."

The words struck exactly where she intended.

No cruelty. No comfort either.

I had looked because I was afraid. I had also looked because part of me preferred fear with moral importance to the simple embarrassment of being outplayed.

Soren waited with my cord in his hand.

Soren: "Point stands."

Elira: "Obviously."

I returned to the start mark and tied the cord again. My face felt warm.

No ancient system woke. No one died. The shame remained the size of a lost point.

I had forgotten feelings were allowed to stay that small.

Across the square, Leon finally caught Cassian's cord. He did it without deception: one failed reach, a second that Cassian mocked, then a third timed exactly when Cassian leaned into the mockery.

Leon held the cloth up.

Leon: "One." Cassian stared at him.

Then laughed, real and sharp.

Cassian: "There you are." Elira marked Leon's point.

Rhea checked the garden clock.

Rhea: "Thirty-two minutes until medical preparation for hearing."

Aira: "President Valmont has entered the dangerous phase where she pretends timing is not enthusiasm."

Rhea: "Twenty-nine minutes if commentary continues."

Aira closed her mouth with both hands. Round three.

Soren had two points. Leon had one. Cassian and I had none.

I tried not to want one.

That failed before Aira lowered her hand. Wanting changed the square.

Not into a battlefield. Into a problem with edges I could touch.

Soren expected me to overcorrect after the cough. He guarded his cord and left his forward shoulder open, inviting an attack he could turn. Leon watched Cassian. Cassian watched everyone with the relaxed attention of a cat at an unsecured banquet. I moved toward Soren.

He shifted to close his right side.

I let my eyes follow the cord. My hand did not.

At the last step, I planted short and reached across for the loose end at his left, where the knot had rotated during the previous round. No magic. No impossible perception. Just cloth moving differently after use. Soren caught my wrist. Grip was not prohibited.

Neither was turning with it.

I followed the pressure instead of resisting. His hold pulled me half a step closer. My other hand closed around the cord and came away with it.

For one second I only stared.

Blue-gray cloth. Ordinary weave. Warm from another person's coat.

Elira struck the score slate with the chalk.

Elira: "Aerlen, one."

Something rose in me before caution could interrogate it. Joy. Small, bright, embarrassing joy.

Then guilt arrived because Cael was dead, Elira was still pale, Krail's petition waited on the table, and somewhere Noctis was already preparing the next cruelty. Happiness seemed indecent beside unfinished harm.

Soren looked at the cord in my hand.

Soren: "You saw the knot turn."

Haru: "Yes." My breath steadied against the cold air.

Soren: "Good."

He did not tell me the point meant more than a point. That saved it.

Behind him, Talen had seen my expression change.

Talen: "You are allowed to look pleased." I looked toward him.

Talen: "It does not amend the dead."

His braced hand rested against the metal bowl. He did not speak like a lesson. He spoke like someone who had once dropped a cup and spent years believing every later pleasure had to justify the sound.

I let the joy stay.

Only for the walk back to the start mark.

It was enough to remember the shape.

Round four began with Soren at two, Leon and me at one, Cassian still at zero and therefore most dangerous.

Cassian stood casually near the boundary.

Leon: "You are planning something irritating."

Cassian: "I am hurt by your certainty."

Leon: "You moved your knot to the back."

Cassian: "I am adapting. You used to praise that when Haru did it."

Leon: "I did not."

Aira: "Historical note: he absolutely did not." We moved.

Soren came for me with none of his earlier patience. I barely kept the cord through the first exchange. His hand brushed my coat. I turned inside the reach, and he adjusted before my foot finished landing.

For three steps, the square narrowed to timing.

No Black Circle. No concealed reserve. No terror that winning would reveal what I was.

Just a better duelist making me work. I almost laughed.

Soren heard the breath and smiled once.

That was when Cassian took his cord.

He had crossed half the square behind us, using the contest exactly as he had used Soren against Leon. His fingers caught the cloth at Soren's waist and pulled. Cassian held it overhead.

Cassian: "Beauty remains admissible."

Talen: "Both feet inside. Unfortunately." Elira marked the slate.

Elira: "Veyr, one."

Soren looked at Cassian, then at me.

Soren: "I was watching the wrong threat." Cassian bowed.

Cassian: "Put it on my family crest."

Leon: "Your family crest already means that." Cassian clutched his heart. The garden laughed.

Rhea did too, though hers escaped as one breath before she turned it into a cough. Aira saw. She did not write it down.

That might have been the kindest record decision she made all week.

We started a fifth round.

Leon changed stance. Cassian stopped smiling. Soren retied his cord higher. I found myself studying the frost seams for footing instead of exits.

Elira leaned forward with the score slate, gold hair bright under the thin sun. Her face was tired. Her attention was not. Talen called the first boundary. Aira began a commentary comparing Leon's shoulders to a government filing cabinet.

Then Maelin rang the metal spoon against Talen's bowl.

The note cut through the square.

Maelin: "Done."

Four competitors stopped with four different expressions of objection. Maelin looked pleased.

Maelin: "A complete victory."

Elira: "The score is unfinished."

Maelin: "Yes." She noted the pulse reading on the crystal. Soren loosened his cord.

Soren: "Good."

Leon: "Good?"

Soren placed the cloth back in the box.

Soren: "Unfinished is not erased."

No one turned the sentence into a speech.

We gathered the cords. Cassian tried to claim moral victory and was denied by every available authority. Leon insisted his point against Cassian should carry into any resumed session. Elira told him standings did not change under the registration card he had watched Rhea inspect. He argued with the card anyway.

Talen dried the bowl himself.

Soren asked before taking the wet cloth from him.

By the time the others returned toward the house, the garden clock showed eleven thirty-one.

Soren remained at the low wall overlooking Lake Velis. Talen sat on the stone bench nearby with his brace laid open across his knee so the hand could rest without weight. Elira stayed in her chair while Maelin went inside for the medicine she had already warned would taste punitive. I should have followed.

Soren looked at the practice cord still in my hand.

Soren: "If the brackets resume, do you want to compete?"

The question was too ordinary for every answer it touched.

Haru: "Aurelis' position depends on the Council review."

Soren: "I did not ask for Aurelis' position."

The lake moved below us. Dark water under a sky that had not decided whether to snow. I tried again.

Haru: "My participation could turn the bracket into classification evidence. If I win, it becomes proof that Black Circle students cannot compete safely. If I lose while limiting output, it becomes proof that concealment corrupted the standings. If I withdraw-"

Soren: "That is still the public answer."

His voice was not unkind. It was exact enough to leave me nowhere impressive to hide.

Elira watched me over the top of her blanket.

She did not answer for me.

Haru: "I want one match where losing costs pride instead of a life."

The sentence left more of me exposed than any Black Circle manifestation.

Haru: "I want to be angry about a point. I want to practice until something ordinary improves. I want to face someone who wants to beat me without owning what winning means afterward."

Soren's scarred fingers rested on the garden wall.

Haru: "And I do not know if that match exists for me now."

Soren looked toward the square where our footprints crossed and recrossed the frost.

Soren: "It did for one point."

Haru: "There were no relays."

Soren: "Then relays are part of the problem. Not the point."

He did not promise Valemere could protect the distinction. He had already learned what institutions did to clean matches after the fact.

Soren: "I have not withdrawn. The bracket can remain suspended without becoming dead. Your answer can too."

Talen flexed his bare fingers. The tremor was smaller now, not gone.

Talen: "Everyone assumes I want to return." Soren turned toward him.

Talen: "My family calls it reclaiming my future. My instructors call it recovery. Reporters call it courage because they do not have to hold the cup afterward."

He looked at the water stain on his sleeve.

Talen: "I don't know whether competing again would be desire or an argument with Lucien that I make using my own hand."

Elira: "You do not have to know before your hand does."

Talen's eyes moved to her.

Elira's expression tightened with memory. She had written him after the match, refusing to promise repair. Now she did not offer it in a garden either.

Talen: "What about you?"

Elira: "What about me?"

Talen: "Do you want to return?"

Her fingers rested on the score slate.

The old answer would have been immediate. Elira Vale had built a life from preparation so complete that wanting and duty often wore the same clothes. This answer took longer.

Elira: "I want to know what my magic is when it is not proving I deserved the rank people already gave me."

The gold light at her wrist did not appear. Maelin had forbidden output, and Elira did not need to break the rule to make the question real.

Elira: "Competition may be part of that. It may not. I resent not knowing." Talen nodded.

Talen: "That sounds more honest than courage."

From inside the house, Aira shouted that medicine had arrived and smelled like a disciplinary hearing.

Elira stood carefully. I moved toward her, then stopped close enough to offer and far enough not to assume. She took my forearm. Support. Not rescue.

Talen watched the exchange without turning it into hope for himself.

Talen: "One request."

Rhea had returned to the doorway. Her seal was visible at her wrist, ready to record if he asked. Talen looked at it.

Talen: "Do not enter this morning as testimony." Rhea lowered her hand.

Talen: "The water hold can stay a practice note under my control. The rest stays here. I wanted one hour to spill water badly among students. I do not want the Council improving it."

Rhea: "Granted."

Soren: "Valemere copy remains closed."

Aira appeared behind them with a medicine cup in one hand and stopped herself from reaching for her notebook.

Aira: "I hate personal growth when it is inconvenient."

Talen: "You may record that."

Aira: "Finally."

At eleven fifty-nine, Soren sealed the practice cords inside their box. The score stayed on Elira's slate: Ashvale two. Aerlen one. Varek one. Veyr one. No winner. No adjusted standing. No footnote pretending the missing final round had secretly belonged to whoever looked strongest.

Elira carried one loose cord inside.

She placed it across Krail's petition.

The cloth covered the word containment without erasing it.

The hearing opened at noon through five relays.

Aurelis refused to let Krail summon us into an isolated chamber. Rhea called it a health restriction. Valen called it historical caution. Aira called it not letting anyone put Haru in a fancy jar, then was banned from official phrasing for seven minutes.

So the witness review came to the Lake Velis sitting room instead.

The central mirror opened into the Council chamber. Senna stood at the primary rail. Krail sat above her in a tiered seat of dark glass, handsome in the way a blade could be handsome if polished enough. His hair was iron-gray. His Red Circle crest glowed cleanly at his wrist, contained inside a legal seal so it looked less like power and more like entitlement with manners.

Around him sat delegates from Drakenshard, Valemere, Aurelis, northern civil-service schools, and three minor academies I did not recognize.

Noctis' official seat remained empty.

Its absence watched harder than many faces.

Senna's voice remained steady, fingers resting on the table. "This preliminary session concerns whether emergency restrictions are required before the scheduled distributed witness review. The subject of review is not the classification of Haru Aerlen. It is sequence, risk, and procedural safety." Krail smiled faintly.

Krail: "Magistra Voss is correct. This body must not rush classification. That is why provisional containment is a mercy to all parties."

Leon muttered, "There it is."

The mirror did not carry it. Krail continued.

Krail's voice remained steady, fingers resting on the table. "A young woman died. She was restored through an illegal doctrine corrupted by Noctis. We have all grieved the conduit who paid that cost. But grief cannot blind us to the greater event. An unclassified student manifested force through the public relay network, suppressed multiple systems, altered observable magical law, and now remains in unsupervised intimate proximity to the primary resurrected witness."

The room did not move.

Elira's hand tightened on the arm of her chair.

I wanted to reach for her.

I did not. Not because Krail deserved distance.

Because Elira deserved the space to decide whether she wanted my hand while everyone watched for proof that I had already taken too much.

Her fingers lifted. Palm up.

I placed my hand in hers. Krail's eyes sharpened. Good.

Let him write down the difference.

Senna: "Miss Vale, do you wish to answer the proximity concern?"

Elira: "Yes." Her fingers rested lightly against the stone rail.

Her voice carried through the mirror clearly.

Elira: "I am Elira Vale of Aurelis. Yellow Circle. Primary witness to Dominion Severance. Survivor of Votive Return corruption. Current patient under Senior Healer Maelin Orr. Current partner of Haru Aerlen by my own decision before, during, and after the events under review."

Krail: "No one disputes your dignity, Miss Vale."

Elira: "You dispute my ability to consent."

Krail's smile did not change.

Krail: "Trauma complicates consent."

Elira: "Yes. It does. That is why I am under medical care, why my choices are witnessed, and why I have friends rude enough to make me eat bread before proceedings."

Aira whispered, "History will thank me."

Elira did not look away from the mirror.

Elira: "But trauma does not transfer ownership of my decisions to a Councilor who has never asked me what I want."

The first transcript crystal brightened. Krail leaned back.

Krail: "And what do you want?" The trap opened quietly.

If she said me, they would call it dependency.

If she said safety, they would call me danger.

If she said freedom, they would call it insufficiently supervised.

Elira smiled. Not sweetly. Precisely.

Elira: "I want the Council to stop confusing possession with protection." The second crystal brightened. Professor Valen's eyes warmed.

Senna: "Recorded."

Krail: "Mr. Aerlen."

The sound of my name in his mouth made the Black Circle go very still.

Krail: "Do you accept that your presence creates risk?"

Haru: "Yes." I met their gaze without looking away. Several delegates moved. Krail's smile deepened.

Krail: "Then you concede-"

Haru: "No."

The word cut cleaner than force.

I kept my hand in Elira's because she had chosen it there.

Haru: "My presence creates risk. My absence also creates risk. Isolation created the old Circle Zero failure. Forced separation enabled Noctis to make witnesses into routes. Containment would not remove danger. It would move danger into a room with fewer people able to say no."

Senna's pen stopped. Not because she had missed anything. Because the chamber had.

Krail: "You speak as if you understand ancient catastrophic systems better than the Council."

Haru: "No. I speak as someone the ancient catastrophic systems keep trying to turn into a tool."

The old cold pressure rose. Ozone. Metal.

Behind me, I felt everyone notice and not move away. That was the difference.

Rhea stepped into the mirror's field.

Rhea's voice remained steady, fingers resting on the table. "Aurelis submits a countermeasure proposal. No separation order. No containment demonstration. No isolated classification panel. Instead, distributed proximity logs, voluntary medical review, and open-trigger Black Circle stability observation under witness conditions."

Krail: "You are normalizing the abnormal."

Rhea: "No. I am refusing to make abnormality illegal before it has acted unlawfully."

Cassian murmured, "That goes on a banner."

Leon: "Please do not make banners." Krail lifted one hand.

The chamber lights dimmed with procedural calm.

A second document unfolded above the Council rail. Senna's expression changed.

Senna: "That filing was not in the docket."

Krail: "It arrived under neutral seal."

The empty Noctis seat stayed empty. The document opened anyway.

Black frost laced the edges. The house wards woke.

Elira's ward warmed, then asked a silent question through the open consent lines.

She answered by touching it once. No fear. Recognition.

Krail read the first line before Senna could stop him.

Krail: "Supplemental theory: Black Circle proximity may overwrite witness autonomy through grief-bonded mana resonance."

The words hit the room like a scentless poison.

Aira's notes scattered upward. Leon swore. Cassian's red sigil ignited. Professor Valen went pale.

Because the phrase was not modern. It was old. Older than Krail. Older than Noctis.

The mirror behind Senna blackened from the center outward, and a voice I knew too well entered through the legal seal wearing perfect calm.

Lucien: "Do forgive the interruption. I thought the Council might appreciate a more honest question." Elira stood. Maelin snapped, "Sit down." Elira did not. Neither did I.

The Black Circle opened behind my ribs, not as a blaze, not as grief, but as a door refusing to become a weapon. Lucien's reflected smile sharpened.

Lucien: "If Haru Aerlen's mercy is not domination, prove it while everyone is watching." The Council chamber fractured.

Every transcript crystal turned black.

And in the Lake Velis sitting room, the seven open rings inside Elira's pendant began to sing.

===== EPISODE 20 =====

# Episode 20: **The Trial of Proximity**

The sound inside Elira's pendant was not music.

Music wanted to be heard.

This wanted to be obeyed.

Seven open rings rang in seven different pitches, each one a question sharpened until the air itself tried to answer. The Lake Velis sitting room bent around them. The windows became mirrors. The mirrors became doors. The doors became witness rails, polished black and waiting.

Lucien had not entered the house. That was the worst part.

He had entered the argument.

He had learned, perhaps better than anyone alive, that old systems did not need bodies if procedure would carry them.

The Council chamber remained visible in the central mirror, but only in pieces. Senna stood at the primary rail with one hand pressed to a cracked transcript crystal. Krail's seat glowed behind her, sealed behind emergency glass. Delegates shouted without sound. The empty Noctis chair was no longer empty. Not filled. Occupied by absence.

Black frost formed the outline of a person who refused to spend a body on contempt.

Lucien's voice came through every reflective surface at once.

Lucien: "A simple test. Let the Black Circle remain near the woman it restored through grief and prove her will is untouched."

Elira's hand found the crystal.

The crystal burned warm beneath her fingers. Not hot. Alive. Maelin moved first.

She stepped in front of Elira with no magic raised, only the full authority of someone who had long ago stopped being impressed by catastrophes.

Maelin: "Patient consent is suspended under hostile interference."

The pendant answered with a single low note. Lucien laughed softly.

Lucien: "A healer tries to remove her from the question. How kind. How familiar."

The low note sharpened. Maelin froze. Not physically. Legally.

I saw the spell then.

Not with sight. With the cold taste behind my sternum and the way the old house magic recoiled from its own thresholds.

Lucien was using Krail's petition as a frame and Noctis grammar as pressure, but the engine beneath it was older. A proximity trial. A pre-standardization disaster test built to determine whether a safeguard's witnesses remained people or had become extensions of his will.

It had been designed after fear.

That made it cruel enough.

Noctis had edited it after ambition. That made it worse.

Aira: "Haru?" Her voice was tight.

She had her notebook open, pen already moving despite the room trying to turn documentation into evidence against us.

Haru: "It is testing whether anyone near me can act independently."

Leon: "Again?"

Haru: "No."

The nearest window showed my reflection, but the eyes were wrong. Too black. Too still. Too easy for frightened people to believe.

Haru: "This version tests whether emotional closeness counts as contamination."

The room understood before I finished. Cassian's humor vanished. Rhea's face became marble.

Elira did not look away from the mirror.

Elira: "Lucien is attacking our relationship."

Lucien: "I am examining a public risk."

Elira: "You are hiding behind public language because no honest spell would carry you."

For the first time, the frost outline in the Noctis seat flickered. A tiny thing. Satisfying.

Then the crystal rang again.

The sitting room split into stations.

Not physically. Not fully. Old magic rarely needed to be so crude.

Around us, pale circles appeared on the floor, each open at one side. Aira's station lit blue-white around scattered notes. Leon's flowed in water-thin lines at the windows. Cassian's burned red beneath his chair. Rhea's sharpened into council geometry at the threshold. Professor Valen's formed a record sigil near the bookcase. Maelin's steadied beside Elira's chair.

Mine did not appear. Elira's did.

Gold and black, open at the side facing me.

Lucien: "The trial offers mercy. Each witness may step away from Haru Aerlen's field and answer free of influence."

The floor between us darkened.

A path opened toward the far side of the room. Away from me. Away from Elira.

Away from the table where we had eaten bread and argued and revised the pendant with hands that were still human.

Krail's voice cut through the mirror.

Krail: "Magistra, this is an unauthorized manifestation. I request containment-"

Senna: "Denied pending survival."

I liked her more with every crisis.

Lucien: "Miss Vale. You first."

The path away from me brightened. Elira's breath caught.

The crystal pulsed at her throat.

I felt the trial lean toward her wound. Not her love. Her wound.

It offered an explanation that would make pain simpler: You are afraid because he is near. You want because he is powerful. You stayed because the Black Circle taught your body to return to him.

I knew the shape of it because fear in polite clothes always sounded more reasonable than cruelty. I released her hand. Every witness saw it. So did Lucien. So did Krail.

The Black Circle stirred, offended by the distance.

I kept my hand open at my side.

Haru: "Elira chooses."

Lucien: "A useful line." Elira turned toward me.

For one second, I saw the night of the storm in her eyes. The cut. The cold. The memory of dying through a rescue that had been relabeled until mercy became a wound.

Then she stepped away from me. The room gasped. I did not move.

That was the hardest thing I had done since watching her die.

Elira crossed the floor to the far side of the room. The open gold circle followed her, not dragging, not binding, simply asking whether she would remain herself outside my reach.

She stood alone beside the cold fireplace. The pendant's ringing softened.

Lucien: "Good. Now answer. Do you love Haru Aerlen because you choose him, or because the Black Circle made itself necessary to your survival?"

The question was obscene because it wore philosophy. Elira lifted her chin.

Elira: "I loved him before I knew how much danger surrounded him."

The first open ring dimmed.

Elira: "I chose him before his name became public." The second dimmed.

Elira: "I feared him once, when he showed me the Black Circle. Then I understood the fear was not of him. It was of what the world would do if it saw him as a thing." The third dimmed.

Elira: "I wanted him after I died because being alive returned my body to me. Not to him. To me." The fourth dimmed.

Her face flushed, but she did not look down.

Elira: "And last night belonged to me as much as to him."

Aira made a strangled sound and wrote so hard her pen sparked.

Cassian stared at the ceiling with heroic dedication.

Leon turned red and pretended the window required inspection.

Rhea looked like she was calculating whether dignity could survive friendship. Maelin only nodded once. The fifth ring dimmed. Lucien's frost outline sharpened.

Lucien: "A beautiful declaration. Still within proximity memory." Elira smiled.

Elira: "Then let someone else ask." She turned to Aira.

Elira: "Aira." Aira's station flashed.

Aira: "Oh, excellent. I was hoping the ancient relationship court would notice me."

Elira: "Ask me something Haru would not want you to ask." I looked at her.

Haru: "Elira."

She did not look back. Good. Aira's expression changed.

The joke left because the friendship stayed.

Aira: "Do you ever stay with him because you are afraid he will break without you?" The sixth ring flared.

The room held its breath. Elira's smile vanished.

Elira: "Yes." Her fingers rested lightly against the stone rail.

The ring did not dim. Lucien's silence became interested.

Elira: "Sometimes. More often since the Wounded City. I see him watching the world for threats. I see him making himself smaller so no one else panics. I see the Black Circle answer grief faster than he wants it to. Sometimes I am afraid that if I step away, he will decide the safest version of himself is loneliness."

The sixth ring brightened painfully.

Elira: "But that fear is mine. It is not proof that he owns me. It is proof that I love someone who is wounded too." The light steadied.

Elira: "And when I stay, I am not staying because he cannot survive without me. I am staying because I refuse to let fear teach either of us that love is containment." The sixth ring dimmed.

Aira wiped at her face angrily.

Aira: "Recorded, unfortunately."

Lucien: "One ring remains."

I knew before it moved.

The seventh ring was mine.

It had been waiting in the crystal like a blade wrapped in velvet.

The Black Circle opened beneath my skin. Not wide. Enough.

The room's shadows deepened. The lake beyond the windows turned from blue to black glass. Every open circle on the floor leaned toward me.

Lucien: "Haru Aerlen. If Elira Vale asks you to let her face danger without your intervention, will you obey?" There were easier questions. Would I kill? Would I die? Would I expose myself?

Would I burn Noctis down to its foundations?

Those had answers I could give with enough restraint.

This one found the part of me that still heard Elira's body hitting the Wounded City stone.

I looked at her across the room.

She did not soften the question for me. Because she loved me.

Haru: "No." The seventh ring screamed. Every window cracked.

Krail stood in the Council chamber.

Krail: "There. There is the confession."

I swallowed the cold taste in my mouth.

Haru: "If she asks while coerced, wounded, misled, or relabeled by hostile doctrine, I will not obey the shape of the sentence. I will answer the person beneath it." The scream faltered.

Haru: "If she asks as herself, with risk named honestly, then yes."

The Black Circle pressed against my ribs like a storm wanting permission.

I did not give it.

Haru: "I will hate it. I may fail once and need my witnesses to stop me. I will not pretend love makes restraint easy. But I accept that protecting Elira cannot mean becoming the only door she is allowed to use."

The seventh ring dimmed. Not completely. Enough to breathe.

Elira crossed the room back to me.

Lucien: "Careful. The trial has not closed." She kept walking.

Krail: "Miss Vale-"

Elira reached me and took my open hand.

The seventh ring went dark. Not because distance had been maintained.

Because return had been chosen. The pendant fell silent.

For one heartbeat, the old house became only a house again.

Then the central mirror shattered inward. No glass flew.

Instead, the reflection of the Council chamber folded into a narrow black corridor, and at the end of it stood Lucien Voss in full Noctis uniform, pale hair silvered by frost, eyes colder than any spell should make a living person. Not a reflection. Not fully. A relay-body. Illegal. Dangerous.

Beautiful in the way a perfect lie could be beautiful before it cut.

Lucien: "Then let us test return."

Behind him, hundreds of small lights appeared. Student crests. Noctis crests.

Blue, Red, Yellow, a few green points nearly swallowed by dark.

Cael had not been the only conduit-track student.

Iven Sahl's name burned in my memory from the funeral.

The lights flickered like trapped breaths.

Nera stepped forward before I could.

She had entered at some point during the trial, silent as guilt and twice as pale.

Nera: "Those are students."

Lucien looked at her through the corridor.

Lucien: "Those are reserves." The Black Circle opened.

This time, everyone felt it.

The relay-body stepped through the mirror.

One polished black shoe touched the Lake Velis floor.

Frost spread from the heel in a perfect Noctis sigil. The second shoe crossed after it. Lucien arrived without breath, without warmth, and without enough of a pulse for Maelin's diagnostic charm to recognize him as alive. Not a body.

Enough of one to hurt us.

Nera moved between him and the corridor lights.

Nera: "Do not strike the relay-body."

Cassian already had fire in one hand.

He stopped before throwing it.

Nera: "The reserve signatures are carrying the return load. If the body breaks, the feedback goes through them." Lucien smiled.

Lucien: "Still useful. How reassuring." Nera went white.

He had not raised his voice. He did not need to. One sentence returned years of training to her posture. Shoulders back. Hands visible. Guilt arranged as attention.

Darian stepped beside her and struck his own binding ring against the floor. The sound was ugly. Human. Nera's shoulders lowered. Lucien noticed him then.

Lucien: "Darian Thorne. You always did mistake proximity to courage for possession of it."

Darian: "I brought enough to stand here."

Lucien: "Then spend it."

The relay-body lifted one hand.

Every reserve light behind him screamed.

Not aloud. Through the pendant.

Twelve pulses struck Elira's crystal in different rhythms: panic, cold, channel exhaustion, a child's heart forced too fast by a conduit brace. Elira doubled over. Gold light burst from beneath her collar and scattered across the floor in broken arcs. I caught her shoulder.

The Black Circle surged toward Lucien's raised hand. Nera shouted:

Nera: "Those are their pulses! If you erase the signal, you erase our only route to them." I stopped. Lucien's smile widened.

He had wanted the hesitation.

Then he crossed the room faster than a reflection should move.

Leon threw a water wall between us. Lucien passed through it.

The water froze around his outline and crashed to the floor in his shape after he was already beyond it. Cassian changed tactics before the ice finished breaking. He sent fire along the floor instead of at Lucien, burned the Noctis sigil beneath the relay-body, and severed its cleanest anchor.

Lucien staggered half a step.

Cassian: "You do have feet. I was beginning to think you arrived by arrogance alone." Lucien turned his hand. The burned sigil inverted.

Black frost climbed Cassian's flame and reached his wrist. His Red Circle went dark. He swore, dropped to one knee, and drove the affected hand against the stone before the cold could enter his elbow. Leon flooded the line. Steam exploded between them.

Lucien emerged from it beside Elira.

He did not attack me.

That would have been simpler.

He pressed two fingers against the pendant at her throat. Elira stopped breathing.

The room vanished from her eyes.

Lucien: "Do you remember the exact instant your choice stopped belonging to you?"

Cold spread through the crystal. Elira's body arched.

The pendant projected the Wounded City across every wall: Cael inside the return geometry, Elira stepping forward, the hook closing, my face when her pulse stopped. Not memory as it happened. Memory edited for cruelty.

In this version, Elira smiled when the hook took her.

In this version, I reached too slowly because part of me wanted the Black Circle seen.

In this version, Cael looked relieved to die.

Elira saw all three lies while her body remembered the real pain. Lucien leaned closer.

Lucien: "Choice is only the story survivors tell before someone stronger edits the record." I seized his wrist.

My hand passed through cold light and closed around something solid at its center: a narrow black relay rod hidden inside the body.

Every reserve light behind him flared.

Children cried through the crystal.

I could not crush it. Lucien knew.

He looked at my hand around the rod and spoke softly enough that only Elira and I heard.

Lucien: "There. Your mercy has a handle after all." Elira moved.

Still unable to breathe properly. Still trapped inside the false memory. Still hers.

She drove her forehead into Lucien's face. The relay-body snapped backward.

His fingers left the pendant.

Elira fell against me, dragged in one breath, and raised her Yellow Circle with the next. No elegant ring. No academy form.

Gold fire wrapped her fist.

Maelin: "Elira, no sustained-"

Elira hit Lucien across the mouth.

The impact cracked the relay-body from jaw to collar. Gold light flooded the fracture and exposed the black rod in my hand.

For the first time, Lucien looked surprised by pain.

Elira: "You do not get to tell me what I remember."

Blood appeared at the corner of her mouth. Not from his strike.

From the output tearing through channels that had not recovered enough to carry it.

Maelin caught her as her knees failed.

Maelin: "Done. Your body is done."

Elira tried to raise her hand again.

Maelin trapped it against her own shoulder.

Maelin: "You chose the first strike. I am choosing medical restraint before the second kills you. Be angry later." Elira shook with fury. She stopped.

Lucien touched the crack in his borrowed face.

Gold burned beneath his fingers.

The reserve lights pulsed erratically. The damaged body had begun drawing more from them to repair itself. Aira saw the pattern.

Aira: "He is cycling through the lights. Third, seventh, twelfth-then back to third."

Nera looked into the corridor.

The seventh light flickered blue-white. Iven.

Nera: "The relay has a registry index. If we take one cycle, we can keep the route after he closes it."

Rhea: "Method?"

Nera was already unfastening the scorched binding ring from her wrist.

Nera: "I enter. Darian anchors me. Aira calls the cycle." Darian grabbed her arm.

Darian: "No. We enter."

Nera: "The corridor recognizes my command history."

Darian: "And Lucien recognizes your guilt."

They stared at each other.

No time for a perfect answer.

Rhea made the choice reviewable instead.

Rhea: "Nera enters one body length. Darian maintains physical anchor. Leon controls the threshold. Cassian burns only floor sigils. Aira calls retreat whether or not the registry is secured."

Nera: "Accepted."

Darian: "Accepted."

Lucien laughed through the fracture in his face.

Lucien: "Aurelis turns panic into committees with admirable speed."

Rhea: "And Noctis turns children into batteries. I prefer our delay."

Leon drove water into the shattered mirror frame. It spread in a blue border around the corridor, giving the threshold a physical edge. Cassian burned the frost away from Nera's path in short red bursts. Each flare made his darkened wrist spasm. Aira watched the lights.

Aira: "Third. Seventh. Twelfth. Third. Seventh-go."

Nera stepped into the corridor.

Darian locked both arms around her waist.

The cold tried to pull them apart by making each body feel like the other's restraint. Nera cried out. Darian loosened his grip enough for her to choose it again. Nera reached. The seventh light recoiled.

Nera: "Iven Sahl. Noctis first-year. Conduit track. Thermal brace sensitivity. Cael Nox witness link." The light steadied.

A small slate of black glass formed beneath it. Lucien moved toward her.

I stepped between them with my hand still closed around the relay rod. Not crushing. Holding.

The Black Circle turned once under my skin. Every shadow in the room aligned behind me. Lucien stopped.

Haru: "You wanted to know what I protect."

The words came out colder than I intended.

Haru: "Watch."

Behind me, Nera tore the black slate free. The corridor convulsed.

Aira: "Retreat!"

Darian pulled. Nera came backward with the slate against her chest. The threshold snapped at her leading shoulder. Leon closed his water border around it, but one blade of black glass crossed before the seal completed.

It cut Nera from collar to upper arm. Darian caught her.

Maelin could not leave Elira.

Rhea threw a red compression seal across the wound. Temporary. Painful. Enough.

Nera did not look at the blood.

She looked at the slate. One name remained visible.

**IVEN SAHL - ACTIVE RESERVE ROUTE / LOCATION WITHHELD**

Under it, eleven registry positions flickered without names. Not a rescue. A route.

Lucien saw what she had taken.

The warmth left his expression completely.

He reached through the cracked relay-body and closed his hand around the rod I held.

For one second, we both touched the same tether.

His fingers were cold enough to burn.

Lucien: "You have mistaken one stolen name for progress."

Haru: "You noticed the theft." His eyes sharpened. Good. I opened my hand.

He expected resistance. My release made him pull too hard. The relay-body staggered backward into its own corridor. Cassian burned the last floor sigil. Leon slammed the water border shut.

Elira, pale in Maelin's arms, lifted two fingers.

Gold light struck the cracked mirror at its weakest point. The relay-body shattered inward.

Every fragment carried Lucien's face for one falling instant.

Then the pieces became frost and blew back through the corridor without touching the students behind it. The twelve lights remained. So did Lucien's voice.

I crossed back to Elira. Maelin kept one arm around her ribs but did not block the hand Elira held out for me.

Elira's hand tightened around mine. Not to stop me.

To remind me where I stood.

The frost remaining inside the broken mirror formed Lucien's smile.
