The Council chamber returned in broken fragments.

Senna's voice came through static.

Senna: "Emergency session suspended. Aurelis, secure your students. All schools, lock conduit registries now."

The mirror went black. No one moved.

Maelin broke the stillness by throwing a roll of bandage at Leon's head.

He caught it on reflex.

Maelin: "Compression on Nera's shoulder. Darian, keep her sitting. Cassian, show me your wrist. Elira, if you raise that hand again I will personally redefine autonomy as remaining conscious." Everyone moved.

Pain made the room honest faster than procedure had.

Nera sat against the overturned table with Rhea's red seal still clamped over the cut. Blood soaked the collar of her borrowed coat. Darian held the bandage where Leon placed it and counted each breath she tried to hide.

Cassian's right hand would not produce flame. The skin was unburned, but black frost remained beneath the Red Circle line like ink trapped under glass.

Elira's pulse skipped every seventh beat.

Maelin heard it and became terrifyingly quiet.

Maelin: "No more Yellow output today. Not one spark."

Elira: "The corridor-"

Maelin: "Closed. Your channels are not."

Elira looked at the black slate in Nera's lap.

The registry positions were fading.

Iven's name remained. The eleven unnamed lights did not.

Aira saw the first disappear.

Aira: "No. No, no-Darian, angle the slate toward me."

Darian: "I am holding pressure."

Leon took the slate without removing his hands from Nera's shoulder. Water rose from his wrist in a thin transparent sheet and held the glass at eye level. Aira opened her notebook. The second light vanished.

Nera: "I knew it." Darian tightened the bandage.

Darian: "Then know the next one."

Cruel wording from anyone else. From him, a rope.

Nera looked at the slate.

Nera: "Third: Green. Weak thermal return. Younger than Iven. Fourth: Red, brace distortion on the downbeat. Fifth: Blue-" Aira wrote.

Mira was not there. The Green copy table was days away at Aurelis. No duplicate hands waited automatically.

So Rhea tore the Council petition in half and wrote on the blank backs.

Professor Valen took the margins of her historical notes.

Cassian, unable to cast, used his left hand to copy colors onto the paper wrapping from the food basket.

Leon held the slate steady with water because both physical hands were needed for Nera.

Elira reached for a page.

Maelin slapped her fingers away.

Maelin: "You are a patient."

Elira: "I can dictate." Maelin considered the compromise.

Maelin: "Dictate."

Elira tracked the visible order while Nera named cadence.

Elira: "Sixth position dimmed before fifth. Record independent interruption. Seventh is Iven. Eighth-Blue, paired flicker with ninth."

The slate grew cold enough for Leon's water support to freeze.

He swore and increased pressure. The glass cracked.

Aira: "Do not let it split through a position."

Cassian looked up from his food-wrapper copy.

Cassian: "That is usually my department."

The joke lasted one breath.

Then the tenth light vanished. Nera lost sequence.

She stared at the blank position, breathing too fast.

Nera: "I do not know."

Nera: "I should know."

Work small enough to survive panic. Nera swallowed.

Elira: "It changed before disappearing."

Nera: "Conduit masking."

Aira wrote the phrase across three pages.

The slate erased everything except Iven Sahl's name.

Then a Noctis seal surfaced beneath it.

**UNAUTHORIZED REGISTRY POSSESSION**

Black fire caught the lower edge.

Leon released the water support before the flame could travel into his Circle. The slate dropped.

Haru: "Do not touch it."

Inside remained one name and eleven missing positions.

Across the room remained five incomplete copies made on a petition, historical notes, food paper, Aira's notebook, and Maelin's medical wrapper.

The copies disagreed on two colors and three pulse orders.

They agreed children were there.

Nera looked at the mess of paper.

Nera: "Noctis will call this corrupted extraction."

Rhea locked the evidence case.

Rhea: "It is corrupted. We extracted it while injured from a hostile relay-body using child conduits. Corruption is part of the evidence." Aira underlined the sentence.

Maelin finished binding Nera's shoulder and moved to Elira.

Elira did not resist when the healer guided her onto the sofa. That frightened me more than resistance would have.

Maelin: "You bought one strike. Your body charged interest."

Elira touched the blood at her lip.

Elira: "He felt it."

Maelin: "So did you. Only one of you is my patient." Elira looked at me. Not proud. Not apologetic.

Furious that Lucien had made violence necessary and unwilling to let fury erase the cost.

Elira: "Record both." Aira did. Then Rhea spoke.

Rhea: "Recovery leave is over."

Elira looked at the silent crystal. Then at me.

Her eyes were gold, steady, alive, and furious.

Elira: "Then we go home."

---

Going home required paperwork.

That felt obscene for several reasons and necessary for several worse ones.

Rhea did not let anyone rush for the carriage until she had three sealed records, two medical clearances, one Council travel objection, and Aira's handwritten sequence summary copied twice because the first copy had jam on the corner.

Aira: "History can survive fruit."

Rhea: "History can survive legibility." Aira copied it again.

Elira sat near the window while Maelin checked her pulse for the fourth time in ten minutes. The trial had not wounded her in the visible sense. That almost made it easier for frightened people to ignore what it had done. Her hands were steady. Her breathing was controlled. Her pendant was quiet.

But her gaze kept returning to the empty space where the BELOVED door had stood.

I saw it because I was watching too closely.

Then I made myself look away before watching became another form of taking. Maelin noticed. Of course she did.

Maelin: "Progress. Irritating, but progress."

Haru: "Was that for me?"

Maelin: "Unfortunately."

Elira's mouth moved toward a smile. It did not arrive.

I crossed the room slowly and stopped before I reached her chair.

Haru: "May I?"

The question changed the air. Not because no one had heard consent before.

Because the entire morning had been a machine designed to make asking feel theatrical.

Elira looked up at me.

Elira: "Yes." Her chin rose, clear and deliberate.

I knelt beside her chair. Not because she was fragile.

Because I wanted to be lower than the argument for once.

Haru: "I am sorry he used the archive."

Elira's fingers tightened once on the chair arm.

Elira: "He did not use the archive." I waited.

She looked toward the mirror.

Elira: "He used the idea that private things become dirty when hostile people see them."

The room quieted around that. Aira stopped writing. Leon looked down.

Cassian's expression lost its easy edge.

Elira's voice stayed calm, which meant each word had been chosen from somewhere painful and exact.

Elira: "The Moonlit Archive is still ours. Lake Velis is still ours. Last night is still ours. The fact that he tried to drag them through a trial does not make them his evidence."

I bowed my head. Not in defeat. In recognition.

Haru: "Then I will remember that before I get angry."

Aira: "Before?"

Haru: "During." Elira touched my shoulder.

Elira: "Better."

The mirror chimed again, and every person in the room looked ready to destroy it.

Senna's seal appeared in the glass with visible strain lines.

Senna: "I am reconnecting under emergency witness relay. This line is clean for approximately ninety seconds."

Rhea stepped into frame immediately.

Rhea: "Report."

Senna: "Krail is attempting to reframe the hostile interruption as evidence that Lake Velis proximity creates uncontrolled old-system events. I have suspended session before he could file the phrase into record."

Rhea: "Can he reopen?"

Senna: "Yes. Not today if I continue being professionally unpleasant." Aira whispered, "Notebook Senna." Rhea ignored her.

Senna's eyes moved to me.

Senna: "Mr. Aerlen, the Council will ask why you did not destroy the hostile corridor when Noctis student reserves appeared."

Haru: "Because I did not know what would happen to the students connected to it."

Senna: "Good. Say exactly that later. Do not improve it." Elira almost smiled again. Senna looked at her.

Senna: "Miss Vale, the Council will ask whether the proximity trial altered your stated feelings toward Haru Aerlen."

Elira: "It clarified my anger." Senna paused.

Senna: "That is acceptable if followed by medical confirmation."

Maelin leaned toward the mirror.

Maelin: "Her anger is stable." Senna blinked once.

Senna: "Noted." The mirror crackled.

Senna's image distorted around the edges.

Senna: "Final point. Noctis has sealed its official dormitory wing from outside registry audit. Their explanation is internal contamination control. We recovered partial crest signatures independently of the registry fragment you took from the corridor."

Nera, who had been silent near the door, lifted her head.

Nera: "That means they moved students before sealing." Darian's jaw tightened.

Senna: "We suspect so." Nera's binding rings clicked.

I had never heard them do that before without magic.

Just metal reacting to a hand becoming a fist.

Nera: "Send the signatures. We need to match them before Noctis moves the routes again."

Senna: "Not yet. We have partial crest signatures."

Rhea: "Nera."

Nera did not look away from the mirror.

Nera: "I know the conduit track. I know how they hide weak crests under training labels."

Senna studied her for half a second. Then nodded.

Senna: "Through Aurelis protection channel only."

The mirror flashed. Twelve small lights appeared above the table, each one blurred by missing identity.

Blue. Blue. Green. Red. Blue. Yellow. Green. Blue. Red. Blue. Yellow. Green.

Twelve students. Not numbers. Not reserves.

People whose names had been rubbed thin enough that the lights had to stand in.

Nera approached them as if walking toward a grave. Darian stood beside her. Elira stood too.

Maelin made an objection with her entire face.

Elira ignored the face and did not cast. That was compromise.

Nera touched the air beneath the first blue light. Her mouth tightened.

Nera: "First-year." The second.

Nera: "Second-year. Binding-compatible."

The third, green. Nera flinched.

Nera: "Too young for conduit track." No one spoke.

The seventh light pulsed weakly.

Iven's name already existed on the stolen corridor slate. This was the first outside signature that could confirm the route instead of merely repeating Lucien's architecture. Nera stared at it.

Nera: "That one matches."

Darian: "You know him?"

Nera's voice became very quiet.

Nera: "Cael once gave a thermal charm to a first-year who cried during winter endurance drills." Elira closed her eyes.

Haru: "Iven Sahl." Nera nodded once.

The green light flickered blue-white.

Independent recognition did not free him.

But it made him harder to erase. Senna's image fragmented.

Senna: "Time. Return to Aurelis. The academy has better old-system shielding than Lake Velis if Noctis pushes again."

Senna: "Under witnesses." The mirror went dark.

Nera remained beside the lights until they faded.

Then she turned toward me.

There was fear in her face. Not of me.

Of what she needed from me.

Nera: "If Lucien uses them the way he used Cael..." She could not finish.

She did not need to.

The Black Circle waited for my answer. So did the room.

I wanted to promise impossible things. No one else will die.

I will tear Noctis open.

I will bring them all back.

Every one of those promises had teeth.

I made myself give the only answer that did not pretend I owned the future.

Haru: "We find the route first."

Nera's face twisted. Not satisfied. But steadied.

Haru: "Then we decide with witnesses present."

Elira's hand slipped into mine.

This time no trial answered.

Only the house, old and tired and perhaps a little relieved, releasing the door wards one by one for departure.

Outside, Lake Velis shone under afternoon light.

The place where we had learned to be close did not ask us to stay.

It had done its work.

Now it let us leave.

The carriage arrived under a sky that could not decide whether to rain. That felt appropriate.

Lake Velis had given us sunlight, storms, moonlight, and one morning honest enough to hurt. Now the clouds sat low over the road while Rhea checked the travel seals, Maelin argued with the luggage because apparently even bags could be medically irresponsible, and Aira tried to organize everyone into an order that did not accidentally imply Haru was either prisoner or king.

Aira: "This is harder than it looks."

Leon: "No one thought it looked easy."

Aira: "Excellent. Then my suffering is visible."

Cassian leaned against the carriage door, watching the lake.

Cassian: "Do we need a formation name?"

Rhea: "No."

Cassian: "Witness diamond?"

Rhea: "No."

Cassian: "Protective social rhombus?"

Leon: "That one offended geometry."

Elira stood beside me on the porch steps, wrapped in a pale cloak with the crystal visible at the throat. The wind moved her hair across her cheek. She did not fix it immediately. That small delay made me think of the bedroom, the morning, the way ordinary gestures could become unbearable when the world kept trying to translate them into public risk.

I lifted my hand, then stopped. Elira glanced at me.

Elira: "You can move my hair."

Aira, from the carriage, made a strangled noise and turned away with excessive dignity.

I gently tucked the strand behind Elira's ear.

The pendant did not flare. No trial opened. No ring sang.

No Council crystal recorded the motion unless Aira was lying about looking away, which was possible. Elira's eyes softened.

Elira: "See?"

Haru: "I know."

Elira: "Practice knowing."

The phrase had become a wound and a cure. I nodded.

At the bottom of the steps, Nera stood apart from the others with Darian beside her. She kept looking toward the west, though Noctis was not visible from the lake house. The blurred crest signatures Senna had sent remained in her posture. Twelve lights. One blue-white trace that might be Iven. Others she did not yet know how to name. Elira noticed too.

She walked down the steps before Maelin could object.

I followed, not too close.

Nera straightened when Elira approached.

Old Noctis training, still moving in the body after the mind had crossed the line.

Elira did not comment on it.

Elira: "You are allowed to be afraid for them without becoming responsible for everything Noctis did." Nera's mouth tightened.

Nera: "That sounds generous."

Elira: "It is not. It is practical. Guilt makes bad maps."

Darian looked at her then, surprised.

Nera let out one breath that was almost a laugh and not one at all.

Nera: "Aira said something similar with worse phrasing."

Aira called from the carriage, "My phrasing survives under pressure."

Rhea: "Your phrasing causes pressure."

Elira smiled faintly, then looked back at Nera.

Elira: "When we find them, you will see things you wish you had stopped earlier." Nera's eyes shone.

Nera looked at the crystal.

At the place where Dominion had killed her.

Elira did not hide it.

Elira: "We keep moving anyway."

Nera nodded once. No absolution. No forgiveness forced from the future. Only direction.

When we entered the carriage, I sat beside Elira because pretending otherwise would give Krail's argument more respect than it deserved. Rhea sat opposite us with documents. Aira wedged herself into the corner with notebooks. Leon took the window. Cassian took the seat nearest the door because he said it had the best dramatic exit potential and Dren, riding outside, told him to stop narrating.

As the restoration house receded behind us, Elira's hand found mine beneath the edge of her cloak.

Hidden from the road. Not hidden from witnesses. Aira saw.

She said nothing. That was how I knew she understood.

The carriage turned toward Aurelis, carrying the last warmth of Lake Velis into a world that had already begun preparing arguments against it.

The road back did not stay quiet. It tried.

At the first ridge marker, every carriage wheel locked.

Wood screamed against the axle. Horses reared. Dren shouted from the driver's bench while the carriage slewed sideways toward the drainage drop.

Leon hit the window with one palm. Water burst from the roadside ditch and braced the downhill wheels.

Cassian reached for flame with his frost-darkened wrist. Nothing answered.

He switched hands without comment and burned through the iron locking pin under the nearest axle.

Nera looked past them to the road marker.

Its gold travel crystal had turned black around one sentence:

**RETURNING NOCTIS WITNESSES: HOLD FOR ORIGIN REVIEW**

Nera: "Do not break the marker. The hold transfers to the people named."

The carriage slid another foot.

Elira tried to stand. Maelin's remote medical seal flashed from the following carriage before her feet reached the floor.

Elira sat back down with visible hatred.

Rhea threw open the door.

President Valmont: "Who can release the axle without answering origin?"

Aira was already halfway under the bench, pulling luggage straps free.

Aira: "No one releases it. We redistribute weight, lift the locked wheels, and move the carriage past the marker without asking permission."

Leon: "That is your plan?"

Aira: "My plan is ropes. Develop criticism while tying one."

Darian and Leon looped the straps through the roof brace. Cassian cut the second pin. Rhea anchored the rope to a roadside cedar with her limited seal. Nera climbed onto the uphill step so the hold spell would keep tracking her instead of shifting to the injured carriage behind.

The marker brightened around her name. She looked afraid.

She stayed on the step.

Haru: "Ready."

I took the rope with everyone else. No Black Circle. Shoulders, boots, wet leather, and six people pulling badly together.

The locked side of the carriage rose.

Dren drove the horses forward.

For one breath, the vehicle balanced on two wheels above the drop. Elira gripped the seat. Aira shouted left when she meant right, corrected herself, and no one died of the error. The carriage lurched beyond the marker and slammed back onto the road. The black hold vanished.

Nera jumped down after it cleared and nearly collapsed. Darian caught her injured side carefully.

Cassian looked at his useless casting hand, then at the smoking pin he had cut with the other.

Cassian: "Heroics remain banned. Improvised road engineering appears legal."

Aira: "Barely."

Behind us, the marker returned to gold as if nothing had happened.

Rhea copied the hostile sentence before we continued.

This time the road understood that holding people and holding wheels were different only if someone survived long enough to write the distinction.

Before the carriage moved again, Nera scratched Iven's name into the harmless side of the road marker with a loose stone.

Not location. Not custody. Proof that an origin hold had tried to stop witnesses from reaching someone Noctis had already hidden.

The gold crystal attempted to smooth the letters away.

Cassian wedged the burned iron pin beneath the marker and jammed its cleaning charm.

Cassian: "Improvised road engineering. Still legal."

The name remained as we continued toward Aurelis.

For the first twenty minutes, the carriage held the kind of silence that was not empty but full of people deciding which thoughts could survive being spoken aloud. Rain tapped lightly against the roof. The lake vanished behind cedar and stone. The old house wards faded from my awareness one thread at a time until only Elira's pendant remained warm beside me.

Then Leon said, "I am going to ask something unfortunate."

Aira did not look up.

Aira: "That is your natural tone."

Leon ignored her and looked at me.

Leon: "If the Council orders you separated from Elira during the review, what happens?"

The carriage changed. Not because the question was cruel. Because it was useful.

Elira's hand stayed in mine beneath the cloak.

Rhea looked up from the document in her lap.

Cassian stopped watching the road.

Nera and Darian listened from the opposite bench as if the answer might teach them whether crossing from Noctis had truly meant entering a place where hard questions could be asked without punishment.

I considered the easy answer. I won't allow it.

The Black Circle liked that answer.

For that exact reason, I did not give it.

Haru: "I do not know."

Leon frowned. Not disappointed. Thinking.

Haru: "Separation after the Black Circle reveal is not the same as secrecy before it. Before the reveal, distance protected the secret. Now forced distance could become an old pattern: isolate the safeguard, claim containment is safety, let fewer people challenge what happens next." Rhea nodded once.

Haru: "But if I say separation is impossible, Krail argues Elira is necessary to my control and therefore compromised."

Elira's thumb moved once across my knuckles.

Haru: "If I accept separation too easily, Lucien argues witnesses are decorative."

Leon looked toward the rain-dark window.

Leon: "So there is no clean answer."

Haru: "No." Cassian leaned back.

Cassian: "There is rarely a clean answer. There is usually a best next inconvenience."

Aira pointed her pen at him.

Aira: "Do not accidentally become wise. It will ruin morale."

Cassian: "My apologies." Elira spoke then.

Elira: "If they order separation, I answer first." Rhea's eyes sharpened.

Elira: "Not Haru. Me."

Maelin, riding in the following carriage, was not present to object. Somehow the air objected on her behalf. Elira continued anyway.

Elira: "The question is being framed as whether I contaminate Haru's stability or he contaminates my autonomy. I will not let them debate my presence while treating me as environment."

Nera's face changed. Quiet recognition.

Noctis had made students into environments all the time. Useful pressure. Available conduit. Moral example. Warning.

Darian looked at Elira with something like respect sharpened by grief.

Darian: "They will say trauma makes your answer unreliable."

Elira: "Then Maelin answers second. As medical authority. Rhea third, as student protection. Aira fourth, because records survive things dignity cannot."

Aira placed a hand over her heart.

Aira: "I am moved and insulted."

Elira: "Good. Stay alert."

Rhea was already writing the order down.

Leon looked at me again.

Leon: "And you?"

Haru: "I answer after."

That cost less to say than it would cost to do. Elira heard that too.

She did not praise me.

She squeezed my hand once. The rain grew heavier.

For a while, the carriage wheels made the only steady sound. Then Nera spoke.

Nera: "Noctis teaches that the first answer belongs to the highest authority in the room."

Rhea: "Aurelis frequently teaches the same thing with better curtains." Nera looked startled.

Rhea: "We are not innocent. We are responsible."

The sentence settled over the carriage.

I thought of Aurelis halls, rank seating, students stepping back from me, Green Circle observers learning to write because nobody had given them swords that counted.

Haru: "Responsibility is better than innocence." Elira looked at me.

Haru: "Harder." She smiled faintly.

Elira: "You would choose the harder word."

Haru: "I learned from someone severe." Rhea looked up.

Elira: "He means me."

Rhea: "I assumed."

The carriage reached the first Aurelis road marker near dusk.

Its crystal lit as we passed, then flickered black for one heartbeat before settling into gold.

Everyone saw. No one panicked. Aira wrote it down. Leon watched the road.

Cassian warmed the carriage with a left-handed heat charm while his right wrist remained frost-dark and medically useless.

Rhea sent a coded notice ahead.

Elira kept holding my hand.

And I began to understand that returning to Aurelis would not be a single arrival.

It would be a thousand small choices not to let old fear decide who spoke first.

## Coda: Heroics Banned

Cassian objected to the phrase heroics banned until further notice for exactly nine minutes. Aira timed him.

Cassian: "Some of us have branding."

Aira: "Some of us have casualty projections."

Leon: "You have branding?" Cassian looked wounded.

Cassian: "I have presence."

Elira, pale against Haru's shoulder, opened one eye.

Elira: "You have volume."

That ended the objection more effectively than policy.

For a few breaths, the carriage held laughter so fragile no one leaned on it. Outside, the road back to Aurelis cut through dark fields and colder consequences. Inside, Nera kept naming possible students behind reserve lights until her voice frayed.

Cassian stopped joking first. That was how everyone knew the map had become real to him.

He tapped Iven's name with two fingers.

Cassian: "Fine. Heroics delayed." Aira wrote it down.

Aira: "Progress."

===== EPISODE 21 =====

# Episode 21: **Return to the Academy**

Aurelis did not welcome us back. It braced.

The carriage crossed the eastern bridge in late afternoon beneath a sky too bright for the mood of the academy. Lake Velis fell behind us in silver flashes between cedar trunks. The restoration house disappeared from view as if the world had folded a secret shut.

Elira sat beside me with her hands folded over the pendant.

She had changed into a formal white-and-navy academy uniform with gold trim. Professor Valen had altered the collar herself so the new crystal could rest visible at her throat when Elira chose, hidden when she did not. Today she chose visible. Not for display. For argument. I wore black.

That had not been a decision so much as a lack of patience for pretending Green cloth still meant anything. Aira had looked at the coat, looked at me, and said nothing. That was how I knew the situation was serious.

Leon rode opposite us, one knee bouncing until Rhea threatened to classify it as a hostile vibration.

Cassian leaned near the window, red hair catching the light, eyes sharper than his smile. His right wrist remained wrapped beneath his sleeve after the relay frost; every small movement favored the left hand.

Nera sat with both binding rings covered by plain sleeves and a fresh compression bandage crossing the shoulder Lucien's corridor had cut. Darian Thorne rode beside her, formerly Noctis in all the ways that mattered to politics, newly separate in all the ways that mattered to courage.

Aira had three notebooks open at once.

Haru: "That cannot be efficient."

Aira: "Efficiency is for people whose enemies do not weaponize footnotes."

Elira: "She has a point." I looked at Rhea.

Rhea: "Do not involve me. I have four copies of the same emergency order because three different offices will try to misplace it."

The carriage wheels struck the academy road. My sternum tightened.

Old Aurelis magic rose to meet me from beneath the stones.

Cold pressure. Ozone. Metal. Not hostile. Alert.

The academy knew the Black Circle had returned through its gates. So did everyone else.

Students lined the outer road despite Rhea's order against crowding. Some stood on balconies. Some behind window glass. Some pretended to read notice crystals while staring so hard their mana flickered at their wrists.

Green Circle students clustered near the lower fountain steps. Mira Castellan stood at the front, curly auburn hair tied back, notebook hugged against her chest. Finn was beside her with too many scrolls and an expression of scholarly terror.

When our carriage passed, no one cheered. I was grateful.

Then a Green Circle boy I did not know placed one hand over his crest and bowed. Not deep. Not theatrical.

Just enough to say he had seen the record and understood that seeing did not equal owning.

Others followed. Green first. Then Blue.

A few Red. No Yellow students moved at first.

Then Soren Ashvale, standing near the visiting school arch in Valemere uniform, touched two fingers to his scarred hand and bowed with formal duelist respect. That broke the stillness.

Elira's hand found mine on the carriage seat.

Elira: "Breathe."

Haru: "I am."

Aira: "Barely." I breathed.

The Black Circle stayed quiet.

Instructor Dren met us at the main gate.

His expression had the same stern shape as always, which helped more than kindness might have.

Dren: "Aerlen."

Haru: "Instructor."

Dren looked me up and down.

Dren: "You are taller when everyone stops pretending not to look."

Cassian made a choking sound. Dren ignored him.

Elira stepped down beside me.

Dren's gaze shifted to her pendant, then her face.

Dren: "Vale."

Elira: "Instructor."

Dren: "Medical restrictions?"

Maelin, who had somehow appeared behind him with a healer's bag and the expression of judgment given legs, answered first.

Maelin: "No high-output casting, no extended standing at hearings, no martyrdom, no dueling, no pretending emotional regulation counts as rest."

Elira: "I agreed to most of those."

Maelin: "You agreed to all of them." Dren grunted.

Dren: "Good. Then you will both hate the next hour."

He turned toward the central courtyard.

The path had been cleared. Not empty. Cleared.

Rhea's emergency authority had turned the courtyard into a controlled witness corridor. Student Council members stood at intervals. Faculty wards hovered above the paving stones. Senna's Council seal glowed at the far end near the great fountain, cold stone and the smell of drying ink anchoring the words.

The repaired fountain no longer rippled backward.

It watched normally now. That was not reassuring. Halden waited beside it.

Professor Halden's hair looked more silver than before the funeral. He held no documents, which somehow made him more dangerous.

Haru: "Professor."

Halden: "Aerlen." He looked at Elira.

Halden: "Vale."

Elira: "Professor."

For a moment, all the history between us stood in the air: his suspicion, my concealment, the old observatory, his choice not to isolate me, the way analysis could become either blade or bridge depending on who held it. Halden spoke first.

Halden: "I have been asked to chair Aurelis' internal Black Circle stability observation."

Leon muttered, "That sounds comforting."

Halden's eyes moved to him. Leon straightened.

Halden: "It is not intended to comfort."

Aira: "Spectacular. We are doomed by branding."

Halden ignored that too, but with more effort.

Halden: "I refused twice." That surprised me.

Halden: "The first request came from the academy board, phrased as classification. The second came from Councilor Krail's office, phrased as student safety. I accepted only after Senna Voss amended the charge."

Rhea: "Witness stability, not containment readiness." Halden nodded.

Halden: "My task is to record whether Haru Aerlen remains answerable under pressure. Not to define what he is."

I looked at him carefully.

Haru: "And if I do not?" Halden's mouth tightened.

Halden: "Then we record that too. With witnesses present. Before anyone turns fear into a private room."

That was as close to trust as Halden could survive. I accepted it. The fountain lights shifted.

Senna's remote seal opened above the water.

Senna: "Aurelis, report." Rhea stepped forward.

Rhea: "Haru Aerlen, Elira Vale, and registered witnesses have returned under escort. No hostile Black Circle manifestation during transit. One Noctis origin-hold attempt at the first ridge marker was bypassed and preserved. No proximity contamination observed. A partial hostile registry fragment names Iven Sahl; independent Noctis conduit registry confirmation remains pending."

Senna: "Received. Drakenshard and Valemere have sealed their student registries. Three minor academies report unauthorized relay pings. Noctis Dominion College has not responded to emergency conduit audit."

Nera's face drained of color.

Darian's jaw tightened. Senna continued.

Senna: "We have confirmation that at least twelve Noctis conduit-track students were moved from their registered dormitory wing during the funeral proceedings."

The courtyard noise vanished. Twelve.

Cael had been one. Not the first. Not the last, if Lucien chose.

Nera stepped into the seal's field.

Nera: "Independent confirmation?" Senna hesitated.

Darian: "Magistra."

Senna: "Confirmed. Iven Sahl is among the missing."

The confirmation landed like a second blow against the same wound.

I remembered him at Cael's funeral. First-year, pale, standing with the separate Noctis student group. A thermal charm story carried like proof that Cael had once been kind when no one was recording him. Elira's ward warmed.

Haru: "Lucien showed us reserves."

Halden: "Say that again." I did. This time slower.

I described the corridor, the crest lights, Nera's one-body-length entry, the registry slate she tore free, and Lucien's word. Reserves.

By the end, Dren's hands were fists.

Maelin had stopped pretending she was only there for Elira.

Rhea's council sigil brightened red.

Senna: "Then the Council has probable cause to enter Noctis protective audit."

Krail's voice cut through the seal.

Krail: "The Council has probable cause to contain the extra-classification student who provoked Lucien Voss into threatening children."

The fountain water lost its ripple.

Krail's image formed beside Senna's, crisp and unwelcome.

Krail: "Do not mistake sequence for innocence. Voss is a criminal actor. Aerlen is the event around which criminal actors are now organizing."

Elira stepped forward. Maelin hissed. Elira did not cast. She only spoke.

Elira: "No. Lucien organized cruelty before Haru became public. Talen Mire proves it. Cael proves it. Nera and Oric prove it. Noctis' buried doctrine proves it. You do not get to make Haru responsible for the violence that exposure revealed."

Krail: "Miss Vale, you remain under trauma review." Elira's smile was cold.

Elira: "And you remain uninterested in what trauma actually says."

Students whispered. Not scandal. Support. Krail heard it.

His expression barely changed, but his mana did. Red Circle pressure slid through the remote seal like a blade testing cloth.

The Black Circle answered beneath my skin.

I stopped it. Not entirely. Enough.

Halden's eyes snapped to me.

Haru: "Recorded?" Halden's throat moved once.

Halden: "Recorded." Krail smiled.

Krail: "How cooperative." The fountain cracked.

A black line split the water vertically from rim to base. Not Lucien's frost. Not Noctis lightless. Older.

The old Aurelis system opened a message in the air above the water.

**CIRCLE ZERO SAFEGUARD REVIEW: FIELD RESPONSE REQUIRED**

Mira's notebook fell from her hands. The message continued.

**DOMINION ROUTE DETECTED BELOW ACADEMY INFRASTRUCTURE**

Professor Valen's hand stopped over the record. Halden whispered, "Impossible."

Rhea: "Explain impossible quickly."

Valen: "Noctis should not be able to access the lower observatory after the Foundation locks."

The fountain answered before she could continue.

**ACCESS POINT: OLD TOURNAMENT MEDICAL ANNEX**

Nera made a sound like she had been struck.

Nera: "That is where conduit-track students were evaluated before matches."

Darian: "Where Cael was prepared."

The courtyard shifted around us. Fear became direction.

Lucien had not only threatened missing students.

He had left a route under Aurelis.

Where our witnesses had once trusted the academy to be safer than Noctis.

Instructor Dren turned toward the lower path.

Dren: "Combat team." Leon rolled his shoulders. Cassian grinned without humor.

Aira closed two notebooks and kept the third.

Rhea issued three orders before anyone else inhaled. Elira stepped beside me.

Maelin: "Absolutely not."

Elira: "I am not casting high-output."

Maelin: "You are walking toward a Dominion route."

Elira: "Yes." Her fingers rested lightly against the stone rail.

Maelin: "That was not a loophole." I looked at Elira.

The proximity trial's last question still lived in my ribs.

If she asks as herself, with risk named honestly, then yes. I hated practice.

Haru: "She comes if she chooses."

Maelin looked at me as if deciding whether to be proud or furious.

Elira's hand brushed mine. Not held. Brushed. Enough.

We turned toward the old tournament medical annex as the academy watched the Black Circle walk back into danger with witnesses on every side. For once, I did not hide.

---

The first person who followed us was not a fighter. It was Mira.

She ran three steps, stopped because running after an emergency escort looked too much like panic, then walked quickly with Finn half a pace behind her and a notebook clutched to her chest like a shield she had made herself. Rhea noticed without turning.

Rhea: "Castellan." Mira froze.

Mira: "President Valmont."

Rhea: "This route is restricted." Mira's face flushed.

She looked at me once, then at Elira, then down at the fountain warning still glowing behind us.

Mira: "Then restrict me properly."

Finn inhaled like he had just watched a friend leap off a roof. Aira's eyebrows rose. Rhea turned slowly.

Mira swallowed but did not retreat.

Mira: "Green Circle students have been used as audience, rumor, cover, and public pressure since this began. We were in the gallery when the Foundation Trial tried to make mercy look unauthorized. Our notes mattered then. If there is a Dominion route below the academy, and if Noctis used ordinary students because no one important looks at us first, then you need someone ordinary in the record." The courtyard listened. So did I. Mira's hands shook. She kept speaking anyway.

Mira: "I am not asking to duel Lucien. I would die immediately and embarrass everyone. I am asking to witness what happens to students people consider useful because they are easy to ignore." No one moved.

Then Finn raised one trembling hand.

Finn: "I can index record absence." Rhea looked at him.

Finn visibly regretted being alive.

Finn: "Quietly."

Aira's expression softened with something like pride. Rhea looked to Dren.

Dren: "They stay behind the combat line."

Maelin: "They stay behind my medical line."

Halden: "They stay where their observations remain uncontaminated by direct intervention."

Aira: "That is three different lines and none of you drew them."

Rhea: "Then you will."

Aira: "I regret competence."

Mira's shoulders lowered. Not relief. Assignment.

Rhea stepped closer and placed a restricted observer seal on Mira's notebook. The red council sigil shrank to the size of a coin and settled into the cover without burning it.

Rhea: "You are not there to prove bravery."

Mira: "Yes, President."

Rhea: "You are not there to become evidence of Green Circle disposability." Mira's face changed.

That sentence had found something deeper than fear.

Mira: "Yes, President."

Rhea placed a second seal on Finn's scroll case.

Rhea: "You leave when Maelin, Dren, Aira, or I say leave."

Finn: "Yes." He tapped the stacked receipts into neat alignment. Aira leaned toward him.

Aira: "If I say leave in a very calm voice, run."

Finn: "That seems counterintuitive."

Leon: "It is not."

The second person who tried to follow was a Yellow Circle senior I barely knew.

He wore formal academy white and gold, and the expression of someone who believed emergencies were a stage on which reputation could be recovered.

Senior: "If Black Circle action is occurring under academy ground, Yellow Circle representatives should be present." Elira turned.

The senior went pale for reasons unrelated to magic.

Elira: "Representatives of whom?"

Senior: "Of... senior student rank."

Elira: "No." One word. Quiet. Final.

The senior tried to look past her toward me. That was his mistake.

Elira stepped into his line of sight.

Elira: "If you want to help, report to shelter coordination and make sure frightened first-years are not left alone near rumor crystals."

Senior: "I am a Yellow Circle-"

Elira: "So am I."

The courtyard enjoyed that more than it should have. Elira did not.

Elira: "Power is not the same as usefulness. Go be useful." The senior went. Slowly at first.

Then faster when Maelin glared. I looked at Elira.

Haru: "You enjoyed that."

Elira: "A little."

Haru: "Good." She blinked.

Then smiled despite the route warning, the missing students, and the fact that we were walking toward another hidden room that had learned cruelty from institutions with polished floors.

Those small moments were not interruptions.

They were proof that danger had not taken everything.

At the eastern colonnade, the public reaction changed shape.

The crowd was thinner there, mostly faculty aides, council runners, and students who had pretended to have business near the restricted wing. They did not bow. They did not whisper support. They watched.

One Blue Circle student stepped backward as I passed. Only one step. Enough.

The Black Circle did not stir. My chest did.

Elira saw, but she did not reach for me. Practice.

A small Green Circle girl near the pillar saw the Blue student step away. Her face tightened with fear, then anger, then a child's reckless sense of fairness.

Girl: "He saved Cael."

The Blue student flinched. I stopped.

Everyone stopped because apparently I was now the sort of person whose stopping became an event. I hated that too.

I looked at the girl.

Haru: "I tried to."

The correction hurt the courtyard. It hurt me more. The girl looked confused.

Elira crouched despite Maelin's immediate noise of objection.

Elira: "Cael saved me. Haru tried to save him before that. Both things are true."

Girl: "But Cael died."

Elira's face did not close. Gold eyes, steady.

Alive because of the boy we were still learning how to mourn without making into a lesson.

Elira: "Yes." Her chin rose, clear and deliberate.

The girl looked at me again.

Girl: "Are you angry?"

Every adult in the colonnade lost the next prepared word. I considered lying.

Then decided the child deserved better than a harmless monster.

Haru: "Yes." My breath steadied against the cold air. Her eyes widened.

Haru: "But anger is not an order."

The words landed strangely. Not like wisdom.

Like a rule I had written because I needed it before anyone else did.

The girl nodded with the solemnity only children could give to sentences they might understand later.

Girl: "Okay."

Then she stepped aside. Not away. Aside. Making room.

The Blue student looked at me, shame crossing his face.

I did not forgive him because he had not asked.

I did not punish him because fear was not a crime. We walked on.

At the annex gate, Seraphine Morn waited.

I had not seen her since the funeral aftermath. She wore tactical examiner black with red trim, hair bound severely, one hand resting on the gate ward. Cassian straightened.

Seraphine: "Veyr."

Cassian: "Lady Morn." Seraphine looked at me.

Seraphine: "Aerlen."

Haru: "Examiner."

Her gaze moved to Elira, then the pendant, then the group behind us.

Seraphine: "The gate recognizes three conflicting authorities: Aurelis medical archive, tournament jurisdiction, and visiting school custody. Someone wanted every future investigator to argue at the threshold."

Rhea: "Can you open it?"

Seraphine: "Yes." Her fingers rested lightly against her wrist.

Rhea: "Can you open it cleanly?" Seraphine's mouth curved slightly.

Seraphine: "No."

That was more honesty than comfort. Dren stepped beside her.

Dren: "Then open it loudly."

Seraphine placed her palm flat against the ward.

Red Circle light sharpened around her fingers, not flame, but tactical authority given color. Dren's steadier combat seal joined beside it. Rhea's council mark locked above both. Valen added old Aurelis script under the hinge. Halden, suspicious as breath, refused to let the ward close behind our names without reading the gap between each letter.

Aira wrote every layer down. Mira watched, eyes wide.

Finn whispered, "The verbs are not boring."

Aira: "Then make the nouns work harder." The gate opened.

The smell of the old annex rose out. Antiseptic herbs. Legal ink.

Fear polished until it could pass inspection.

Elira's hand brushed mine once. Not asking. Not clinging.

Marking the last step before descent.

Behind us, Aurelis held its breath.

Ahead, the annex waited with the patience of a place that had been useful to cruel people because no one had known where to look.

I stepped through as Haru Aerlen. The Black Circle followed.

Visible or not, it would have to answer for every inch it moved.

---

The annex did not accept us all at once.

It counted us. That was the first insult. Not by name. By color.

Green. Blue. Red. Yellow. Black.

The final word did not appear on the gate crystal. It formed as absence around my wrist, a dark space where the old system refused to display what the new world had already seen.

Halden leaned close to the crystal.

Halden: "Interesting."

Aira: "Professor, please stop finding ominous things interesting while we are standing in them."

Halden: "Would you prefer I find them dull?"

Leon: "Yes." His jaw set as he shifted his weight forward.

Halden ignored him, which remained one of his core teaching methods.

Valen touched the edge of the gate crystal with one gloved finger.

Valen: "It is not hiding Haru."

For a heartbeat, my false Green Circle appeared.

Then the public Black Circle manifestation image tried to overlay it.

The two did not combine. They rejected each other. The crystal dimmed. Haru Aerlen remained unlisted.

That should have comforted me. It did not.

Systems that refused to classify could still decide you were an exception. Exceptions were often where cages began. Elira's ward warmed.

She did not touch it.

Elira: "Record that the annex failed to classify Haru without prompting him to demonstrate."

Rhea: "Recorded."

Halden's pen was already moving.

Seraphine watched me with a severe expression that felt less like suspicion than measurement under battlefield conditions.

Seraphine: "Can you proceed?"

Haru: "Yes." I met their gaze without looking away.

She did not ask whether I was fine. I appreciated that.

A row of examination badges hung on the wall, preserved under glass. Visiting students had once worn them during tournament medical clearance. Each badge displayed a rank color, school seal, and a narrow strip for temporary health notes. Most were blank. One was not.

**CONDUIT CANDIDATE RESPONSIVE TO EXTERNAL CROWN PRESSURE**

No one spoke.

Because crown did not belong here.

Not yet. Not during the Thirty-Ninth Review, if history had any decency. History did not.

Halden: "Professor."

From old record pressure answering a true sentence.

At the first turn, the walls changed from public stone to private tile. The kind used in infirmaries because it could be washed clean. The air grew colder. Every few paces, a small bracket waited at shoulder height where a temporary monitoring crystal would have been placed during tournaments. Leon touched one bracket.

Leon: "These were used recently."

Blue light crossed his wrist.

The words moved through the corridor like a door closing behind us.

Lucien had not merely left old traps.

Someone had used the annex after Cael was buried.

After Elira was taken to recover.

After the Council thought it had frozen Noctis' official movement.

Rhea's voice became very calm.

Rhea: "Aurelis internal access logs." Aira flipped pages.

Aira: "Already requesting."

Rhea: "No. Already seizing." Aira looked up.

Seraphine: "Aggressive."

Maelin, who had joined us at the annex threshold despite claiming she had no intention of entering ancient nonsense, answered quietly.

Maelin: "Because someone is trying to make captivity sound domestic." Elira's face hardened.

The crystal warmed at her throat.

I did not move first.

Just a teacher walking toward a room that had learned to hide harm under ordinary sounds. We followed.

Beyond the spoon-sound corridor, the first examination chamber opened under overwritten inscriptions.

**VISITING STUDENT RECOVERY ROOM - CROWN FIELD BLOCK**

Cael had been treated here after I stabilized him in secret. The room remembered.

Not emotionally. Stone did not grieve. But mana had habits, and this room's habits had been trained by fear. There were too many anchor points beneath the bed frame. Too many drain sigils disguised as monitoring lines. Too many places a student's body could be measured as capacity instead of pain.

Valen stopped at the threshold and did not enter.

That made everyone else stop too.

Sometimes leadership was not command. Sometimes it was a scholar refusing to put her foot into a room before the room had been named correctly.

Nera: "Noctis teams were told Aurelis required extra safety readings after cross-school matches."

Aira: "Boring verbs survive court."

Lucien's first trap opened under the bed.

It did not explode. It breathed.

Then stopped because Elira's hand caught my sleeve. Not restraining. Reminding. Leon acted first.

Water snapped from his crest in three ribbons, striking the black ring at its open edges. He did not try to overpower it. He lifted the floor moisture, changed the ring's surface tension, and made the ink stumble.
